title: Cloud Computing
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Computing, Mathematics and Engineering
syllabus_overview: This subject provides students with an in-depth study of cloud computing technologies and their use in business. It looks into various standards-based cloud systems and architectures. It further discusses various cloud delivery models and planning for migration to a cloud model. It also discusses governance and security issues in a cloud model, as well as managing the cloud infrastructure.
learning_outcomes: Identify and design an ICT Risk Management strategy for a cloud computing delivery plan to meet business requirements.
Compare and evaluate the ability of different cloud computing architectures to meet a set of given business requirements.
Critically analyse business requirements to plan a migration to a cloud model.
Evaluate a set of business requirements to determine suitability for a cloud computing delivery model.
Compare and critique Service Level Agreements (SLA) that meet the business requirements for a cloud computing plan.

title: Cloud Platforms
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Computing, Mathematics and Engineering
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces students to well-known cloud platforms and examines how compute, storage, networking, identity, and monitoring services are implemented in real environments. Through practical activities, students create, configure, and manage basic cloud resources using industry-standard platforms. The subject emphasises building a strong conceptual understanding of cloud architecture, including the organisation of core services, common naming conventions, and recurring design patterns across providers. Students also learn to interpret cloud dashboards, analyse resource configurations, and recognise foundational security and access control mechanisms. By the end of the subject, students gain both practical confidence navigating cloud platforms and a clear understanding of the underlying infrastructure principles that support them.
learning_outcomes: Identify core services provided by major cloud platforms
Compare how different cloud providers implement similar infrastructure services
Explain how platform services support scalable and resilient digital solutions.
Configure and manage basic cloud resources within a controlled platform environment
Apply basic identity and access management principles within cloud platforms

title: Cloud Privacy and Security
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Computing, Mathematics and Engineering
syllabus_overview: This subject focuses on issues surrounding cloud computing privacy and security and their application to business. It discusses the governance framework that must underpin and define the processes for determining risk, privacy and security issues for an enterprise which uses a cloud model. It will examine the legal and business requirements for privacy, the need for a risk management assessment of all data used in cloud operations, and the use of security controls to manage the assessed risk. It further examines the major cloud deployment and delivery models to determine how these affect the risk management assessment and subsequent security controls when applied to business.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the risk management requirements for a cloud deployment model.
Develop and present a series of proposed security controls to manage the security and privacy of data deployed to the cloud.
Develop and present a cloud governance framework to underpin the cloud operations for an enterprise.
Critically analyse the legal, ethical and business concerns for the security and privacy of data to be deployed to the cloud.
Examine the legal, business and privacy requirements for a cloud deployment model.

title: Coding Fundamentals 1
school: School of Education
syllabus_overview: This micro subject provides an introduction to the essential concepts of coding. In this subject, students will explore the basics of computational thinking and learn how to create simple, interactive programs. The subject focuses on fundamental coding principles, such as understanding sequences, loops, and conditionals, as well as working with variables and basic data structures. Through interactive lessons and hands-on activities, students will develop problem-solving skills and gain confidence in their ability to construct logical solutions. This subject serves as a foundation for more advanced programming studies.
learning_outcomes: Apply basic problem-solving skills in coding tasks.
Apply and execute basic programming constructs such as sequences, loops, and conditions.
Identify and describe fundamental programming concepts and their applications.
Develop and test simple interactive programs.

title: Coding Fundamentals 2
school: School of Education
syllabus_overview: This subject builds on the foundational concepts introduced in Coding Fundamentals 1, taking students deeper into the world of programming. In this subject, students will explore more advanced topics, such as working with functions, handling data, and using libraries to extend the capabilities of their programs. The subject emphasizes problem-solving, algorithmic thinking, and the development of more complex and interactive applications. Through interactive lessons and hands-on projects, students will enhance their coding skills and gain confidence in tackling real-world programming challenges.
learning_outcomes: Debug and test programs to ensure they function correctly and efficiently.
Comprehend the programming environment.
Apply simple algorithms to solve programming problems and create interactive applications.
Work with basic data structures, such as lists and dictionaries, to manage and process information.

title: Cognition
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Psychology
syllabus_overview: This subject provides a grounding in the study and theory of cognitive processes, mainly from an information processing perspective. Topics covered include visual perception, attention, face recognition, memory, imagery, thinking, language, reasoning, problem-solving, and neuro-cognition. Current issues/debates in these areas of cognitive research are also examined. Applications of cognitive psychology are also considered.
learning_outcomes: Use and understand the methodologies of cognitive psychology applied to the study of mental processes.
Identify aspects of the material and personal environment which might affect the efficiency of human information processing.
Demonstrate an understanding of the range and complexity of human mental processes.
Demonstrate an understanding of the dominant paradigm in cognitive psychology ie. the study of the interactions between environmental information and the human processor of information.
Appreciate the many applications of cognitive psychology.
prerequisites: PSY201: Research Methods and Statistics in Psychology
PSY319: Cognitive Processes in Computer Games

title: Cognitive Science
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Psychology
syllabus_overview: The aim of this subject is to enable students to develop intensive research and reasoning skills in the area of cognition. Each year three areas of contemporary research will be examined. Topic areas will closely relate to current research being undertaken within the School. The subject will focus upon the competing theories and models currently under consideration in these areas, the types of research paradigms employed to evaluate these, and an evaluation of recent empirical studies.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of how theory develops in psychology.
Demonstrate a detailed knowledge of the state of contemporary research in at least three critical topics in cognition.
Demonstrate an awareness of the formal and informal interactions that occur between research teams, and how these have contributed to the advance of ideas.
Demonstrate an understanding of how research is conducted in psychology.
Demonstrate an understanding of the interaction between theory and empirical research.
Demonstrate an exposure to problems in understanding brain-behaviour relations.

title: Collaboration for Success
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Business
syllabus_overview: An ability to successfully collaborate is becoming more important in today's workplace, both at an individual and an organisational level. Successful collaboration assists the achievement of mutually beneficial outcomes that exceed the sum of the individual contributions. This subject introduces the key basic components of collaboration that include: having a common purpose or mutual goals; development of trust; sharing of information and resources; joint problem solving and decision-making. Each will be applied through the use of case studies/scenarios at an individual and organisational level.
learning_outcomes: Identify the benefits of collaboration at an individual and organisational level.
Reflect on and compare the merits and limits of various techniques and tools to employ effective collaboration.

title: Collaborative and Person-centred Practice in Exercise Physiology
school: School of Allied Health, Exercise and Sport Sciences
syllabus_overview: Multipathology and complex cases are the most common presentation in clinical practice and safe management of these clients is the cornerstone of Exercise Physiology practice. It is also recognised that telehealth/telepractice is a rapidly emerging mode of service delivery that is helping to facilitate more equitable access to healthcare services for diverse people living in a broad range of geographical locations. Students will be provided with authentic interprofessional experiences to understand how to manage complex, multi-pathology cases in a range of delivery modes. Students will learn to practise in a culturally safe, inclusive, and respectful way while recognising Indigenous Australian health perspectives, decolonising approach to healthcare, and approaches to decision making and change. After completing this subject, students will be able to work with people living with multiple pathologies as part of an interdisciplinary team and deliver appropriate exercise assessments and interventions in a culturally safe manner across a range of service delivery platforms.
learning_outcomes: Identify opportunities to enhance health outcomes for Indigenous Australian peoples through advocacy and change leadership in the profession.
Appropriately refer to other professionals and services, delegate tasks and seek feedback to inform decision-making.

Explain and apply a decolonising approach to decision making to create innovative health services for Indigenous Australian people and their communities with due consideration of all relevant legal, professional, ethical standards and Codes of Practice.
Consider client needs and preferences to determine the suitability for telepractice/telehealth service delivery, and communicate effectively within online practice settings.

Integrate foundational knowledge, pathophysiology and other determinants of health and apply these to inform safe and effective assessments and exercise interventions for individuals and population groups across the lifespan.
Design safe and effective assessments, exercise interventions and behaviour change support for clients with complex presentations including those with multiple comorbidities.
prerequisites: EHR518: Developing the Clinical Exercise Practitioner
EHR519: Exercise Prescription for Cardiopulmonary Conditions
EHR522: Exercise for Metabolic and Mental Health Conditions

title: Collections
school: School of Information and Communication Studies
syllabus_overview: This subject focuses on the management of appropriate information resources for organisations and communities, with particular emphasis on physical and digital materials required to achieve the goals of libraries, archives and related organisations. Attention is given to the assessment of needs, selection, acquisition, evaluation, ethics and deselection of resources, and issues such as policy formulation, budgeting, cooperative resource provision, outsourcing, preservation, electronic publishing and space planning.
learning_outcomes: Analyse historical, contemporary, and emerging trends and issues relevant to collection development practices.
Explain issues relating to the selection and acquisition of information resources.
Exhibit ethical decision making and reasoning to identify solutions to issues such as access, censorship, budgeting, outsourcing and cooperative resource provision.
Identify and discuss the needs of collection stakeholders.
Analyse and synthesise issues associated with disaster management and preservation of collections.

title: Collections

Attention is given to the assessment of needs, selection, acquisition, evaluation, ethics and deselection of resources, and issues such as policy formulation, budgeting, cooperative resource provision, outsourcing, preservation, electronic publishing and space planning.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse complex issues associated with disaster management and preservation of collections.
Evaluate the needs of collection stakeholders in a professional context.
Critically reflect on historical, contemporary, and emerging trends and issues relevant to collection development practices.
Justify creative and ethical solutions to issues such as access, censorship, budgeting, outsourcing and cooperative resource provision.
Apply relevant professional understanding to the selection and acquisition of information resources.

title: Commodity Trade and Pricing
school: School of Agricultural, Environmental and Veterinary Sciences
syllabus_overview: This subject provides an introduction to international agriproduct trade policy and competitiveness. It begins with an exploration of the basic theoretical framework for understanding the benefits of trade, and will explore indepth why there are barriers to trade and why international trade rules are so important. It then examines agriproduct trade policy with a particular emphasis on new trade barriers and the role of the World Trade Organisation. The subject also looks at the importance of managing commodity prices, the various factors that affect commodity prices and analyse a risk management strategy policy.
learning_outcomes: Explain and critically analyse the role of the International Trade Agreements involving agriproducts and the growth of new barriers to trade.
Explain the basis of agricultural protection and evaluate its impact on agricultural trade.
Demonstrate the strategy and basis of the gains from trade.
Evaluate the importance of managing commodity prices, the various factors that affect commodity prices and analyse a risk management strategy policy.

title: Communication and Creative Industries Project 1
school: School of Social Work and Arts
syllabus_overview: This subject consolidates the students' learning over their course of study and provides a foundation for life-long learning. It is organized around thematic project labs which develop professional-standard practice. Students will reflect critically on personal and professional roles and challenges, including the value of cultural diversity in communication and creative industries.
learning_outcomes: Critically reflect on professional issues in communication and creative industries including cultural diversity towards evidenced capacity as a change-maker.
Work independently and as effective collaborative practitioners.
Critically appraise and justify their disciplinarity, interdisciplinarity and transdisciplinarity.
Critique both their own work and that of their peers.
Apply their individual communication and creative practice in any of a number of research-led thematic domains.
Complete a complex project to professional standards for external professional clients, commissioners and audiences.

school: School of Information and Communication Studies

Students will reflect critically on personal and professional roles and challenges, including the value of environmental, political and economic diversity in the communication and creative industries.
learning_outcomes: Critically reflect on professional issues in communication and creative industries including environmental, political and economic diversity towards evidenced capacity as a change-maker.
Work independently and as effective collaborative practitioners.
Complete a complex project to professional standards for external professional-clients, commissioners, audiences.
