title: Legal and Ethical Issues in Health
school: School of Social Work and Arts
syllabus_overview: This subject aims to acquaint students with current ethical and legal issues in relation to, and arising from, modern health care practice. Using a range of ethical principles, the subject examines the role of ethics and law in health care, paying particular attention to issues such as professional responsibility and the duty of care; the rights of patients and consumers of the health system; health information, as well as a range of other current ethical and legal issues. Please note this subject is only offered in years ending in 0, 2, 4, 6, 8.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate their familiarity with legal requirements which bear on biomedical science and research, nursing and allied health care.
Demonstrate their familiarity with professional legal and ethical responsibilities.
Demonstrate their knowledge of ethical theories and principles and their implications for practice in modern health care settings.
Employ forms of ethical reasoning in a variety of health care contexts.
prerequisites: SSC502: Ethics, Law and Medical Science

title: Legal and Ethical Communication
school: School of Information and Communication Studies
syllabus_overview: Professional communicators need to be aware of their public responsibility to engage in sound legal and ethical practice and to understand the legal and ethical issues that apply to their practice. This subject explores the Australian and international regulatory frameworks informing communication practice as well as the ethical requirements and structures relevant to the discipline. The focus is on supporting student's ability to work creatively, ethically and legally in designing, constructing and sharing information and content with others.
learning_outcomes: Identify and communicate an understanding of the Australian regulatory structures relevant to communication, media, content creation and design.
Identify and communicate an understanding of ethical approaches to professional practice in communication and media.
Appropriately respond to problem scenarios relevant to professional practice in communication and media.

title: Legal Frameworks of Employment Relations
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Business
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces students to the historical, constitutional and theoretical underpinnings of the current industrial/employment relations environment in Australia and its associated legal frameworks. It aims to provide students with an understanding of the social, economic and political issues that impact on policy and legislative change and how these are played out in the workplace. Students will be introduced to the various legal and policy frameworks and gain an appreciation of their context, development and application. In particular, students will gain an appreciation for the role of the Fair Work Commission and the impact of FWC decisions on the interpretation and implementation of the legislative provisions. The subject also focuses on non legislative, ethical and human centred approaches to resolving industrial issues including negotiation, conflict resolution and advocacy.
learning_outcomes: Review, evaluate and employ negotiation, conflict resolution and advocacy skills relevant to industrial relations policy and practice.
Analyse and evaluate the historical, constitutional and theoretical underpinnings of industrial relations and associated legal frameworks in Australia.

Evaluate workplace-related scenarios/cases by identifying the relevant issue(s), stating the relevant principles, discussing how these relate to the legal or policy issue(s), and suggesting potential remedies.
Apply the legislative provisions and communicate information to ethically resolve issues related to policy, practices and/or risk to a range of stakeholders using a variety of mediums.

Synthesise issues related to workplace relations, policies, industrial relations parties, and aspects of Australian employment law including modern awards, fair work, work health and safety, workers' compensation and rehabilitation schemes, anti-discrimination and other legislative requirements.

title: Legal Issues in Child and Adolescent Welfare
school: School of Social Work and Arts
syllabus_overview: This subject aims to provide a critical analysis of a range of laws concerned with the care, protection and welfare of children and adolescents. Topics include legal rights, protection and status of children, custody and access, family violence, children in need of care and protection, and adoption. Comparative current law and policy in Australia and overseas will also be considered as well as a brief examination of laws relating to income support for children and adolescents living away from home.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate detailed understanding of the law in relation to promoting and protecting the rights and needs of children and adolescents.
Demonstrate awareness of deficiencies in the law and have some knowledge of the processes of, and trends in, law reform.
Demonstrate a broad understanding of the scope and breadth of laws concerned with the care and protection of children and adolescents, including law in the area of family violence.

title: Level 5 Education subject
school: School of Education
syllabus_overview: EDU51C Level 5 Education subject 8 TCR Catholic Principals' Council Ontario, Canada Principal's Qualification Program (PQP) Part 1 & 2 3702EE, 3702EL, 3702IT, 3702LI, 3702ER Master of Education (with specialisations)

title: Level 5 Unspecified Credit
school: School

title: Liability Claims Management
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Business
syllabus_overview: This subject provides the knowledge and skills to manage and resolve complex insurance claims in liability.
learning_outcomes: Process facultative and treaty claims.
Participate in negotiations related to claims.
Discuss the legal concepts relating to liability.
Settle claims.
Finalise settlements.
Resolve claims disputes.
Review claims settlement policy and procedures.
Evaluate nonroutine claims to accept or deny liability.

title: Liability Underwriting Management
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Business
syllabus_overview: This subject provides the knowledge and skills required to provide liability insurance, survey risk exposure, review and interpret portfolio performance.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the risk.
Discuss the legal concepts relating to liability.
Choose policy wordings.
Review operational performance of portfolios.
Provide quotations.
Negotiate with other related parties.
Evaluate liability quotation slips.

title: Library Services for Children and Young Adults
school: School of Information and Communication Studies
syllabus_overview: Students are introduced to the role of the public library in supporting the learning and information needs of children and young adults. They are also introduced to strategies for facilitating access to library services and for planning, developing and implementing programs for children and young adults. Strategies for marketing and promotion of services catering to children and young adults will also be explored and issues which may impact on the effectiveness of services will be examined.
learning_outcomes: Analyse current research into the information seeking behaviour of children and young adults and apply it to the delivery of effective public library services.
Identify and analyse the needs of a variety of community and cultural groups, age groups and under-served groups of children and young adults in public libraries.
Identify and assess strategies used in dealing with challenges in delivering services to children and young adults in a public library setting.
Identify the developmental, informational and recreational needs of children and young adults and apply them to programs and services in public libraries.
Create and evaluate public library programs and services for children and young adults.
Apply a range of effective strategies to promote the use of materials and resources to provide programs and services for children and young adults in the public library.
prerequisites: INF436: Serving Children and Youth in Public Libraries
INF330: Library Services for Children and Young Adults

title: Library Services for Children and Young Adults
school: School of Information and Communication Studies
syllabus_overview: Students are introduced to the role of the public library in supporting the learning and information needs of children and young adults. They are also introduced to strategies for facilitating access to library services and for planning, developing and implementing programs for children and young adults. Strategies for marketing and promotion of services catering to children and young adults will also be explored and issues which may impact on the effectiveness of services will be examined.
learning_outcomes: Identify and apply knowledge of the needs of a variety of community and cultural groups, age groups and under-served groups of children and young adults in programs and services.
Describe the developmental, informational and recreational needs of children and young adults.
Plan and evaluate programs for children and young adults.
Discuss current research into the information seeking behaviour of children and young adults.
Identify a range of appropriate strategies to promote the use of materials and resources to provide programs and services for children and young adults in the library.
Identify strategies used in dealing with challenges in delivering services to children and young adults in a library setting.
prerequisites: INF436: Serving Children and Youth in Public Libraries

title: Life Span Health Issues and Paramedic Care
school: School of Nursing, Paramedicine and Healthcare Sciences
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces students to the concept of lifespan development and how paramedic practice may be influenced by physiological changes. Students will investigate neonatal, paediatric, obstetric and elderly patients in relation to physical, cognitive and socio-emotional development. Paramedic assessment and management of disorders relating to these life changes are explored within the tutorial, practical and simulated environments.
learning_outcomes: Communicate effectively with a paediatric patient, their family members, and/or carers.
Implement safe, effective, evidence based and patient centred care of paediatric, obstetric and elderly patients.
Accurately identify, assess, and manage the care of obstetric, neonatal, paediatric and elderly patient presentations.
Differentiate normal and complicated childbirth and demonstrate management in simulated settings.

title: Life-stage Considerations: Child, Adolescent and Family Health
school: School of Nursing, Paramedicine and Healthcare Sciences
syllabus_overview: This subject will provide students with a broad knowledge base in the concepts and practices related to family and community health. Health promotion, education and primary health care in a family context are highlighted together with a focus on family dynamics. Using a primary health care framework, this subject explores nursing issues related to the child bearing and child rearing family, and includes: family and society; family structures and functions; child development; families at risk; Indigenous Australian families and those from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds; and models of assessment. A variety of teaching strategies will guide students through various aspects of nursing practice and skill development related to the health and wellbeing of children, adolescents and families; risk assessment, management and minimisation; application of law and ethics in nursing practice, and health education and promotion strategies (for distance education students this will involve a 1 day intensive). Students will undertake an 80 hour workplace learning experience in this subject, which may be undertaken overseas.
learning_outcomes: Recognise and articulate the impact and role of health promotion, health education, primary health and partnership care models (NMBA 2.6, 5.1, 5.2, 5.3, 8.1).

Identify and explain effects of legislation governing nursing practice in the care of children, adolescents and families (aligns with Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia National Competency Standards for the Registered Nurse: 1.1, 1.2, 2.5).
Effectively adjust and evaluate communication to meet the needs of identified target groups while providing education which enables self-care (NMBA 1.2, 2.3, 2.5, 3.2, 5.1, 5.2, 7.7, 9.2, 9.4, 10.2).

Provide comprehensive, safe and effective evidence-based nursing care for children, adolescents and families (NMBA 1.2, 1.3, 2.1, 2.3, 2.5, 2.6, 3.2, 5.1, 5.2, 5.3, 6.3, 6.4, 7.4, 7.7, 8.1, 8.2, 9.2, 9.3, 9.4, 9.5).
Critically analyse epidemiological and health information, and research that impacts on the health of families and communities (with a focus on Indigenous Australians) (NMBA 3.1, 3.2, 3.3, 3.4, 4.1).

title: Linear Algebra
school: School of Education
syllabus_overview: This subject builds on matrix algebra covered in previous studies and includes the topics vector spaces, subspaces, linear transformations, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, inner products and orthonormal bases. Applications of postgraduate level linear algebra, as well as matrix algebra are both covered here.
learning_outcomes: Apply the processes of linear algebra to solve particular problems including: solving systems of linear equations, inverting a matrix, finding eigenvalues and eigenvectors.
Apply and discuss the concepts and processes of linear algebra in relation to a number of real world problems.
Investigate and discuss in depth the mathematical concepts of linear algebra such as: vector spaces, inner products, linear transformations, eigenvalues and eigenvectors.
prerequisites: MTH101: Computer Aided Mathematics 1 with Applications
MTH401: Computer Aided Mathematics 1 with Applications

title: Linear Algebra
school: School of Education
syllabus_overview: This subject builds on matrix algebra covered in previous studies and includes the topics vector spaces, subspaces, linear transformations, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, inner products and orthonormal bases. Applications of linear algebra are also considered.
learning_outcomes: Explain mathematical concepts of linear algebra such as: vector spaces, inner product spaces, linear transformations, eigenvalues and eigenvectors.
Illustrate the use of linear algebra in relation to a number of real world applications.
Apply the processes of linear algebra to solve particular problems including: solving systems of linear equations, inverting a matrix, finding eigenvalues and eigenvectors.
prerequisites: MTH101: Computer Aided Mathematics 1 with Applications

title: Linear Models
school: School of Information and Communication Studies
syllabus_overview: The linear model is all pervasive in the application of statistical techniques to the analysis of data. This fundamental method underpins many others such as nonlinear regression and methods for analysing non-normal data. This subject will give an overview of the linear model and its application in regression and basic experimental design and analysis for data based on independent observations.
learning_outcomes: Recognise situations for which a linear model is appropriate.
Perform design and analysis tasks on recognised software platforms.
Perform basic linear algebra tasks.
Perform the analysis of such experiments and report the results in terms of the original problem.
Critically test any assumptions underpinning the use of the linear model.
Be aware of the limitations of the independence assumption and appreciate the various alternatives available.
Design and check simple experiments.

title: Linux Server Administration
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Computing, Mathematics and Engineering
syllabus_overview: Managing servers is a fundamental aspect of computer science that involves the administration and maintenance of computers that provide web, file, electronic mail, and other networked services. This subject specifically focuses on servers that run the Linux operating system and provides students with an understanding of how to operate them through the command line. Through practical approaches, students will learn how to automate management tasks by writing scripts, analysing and optimising the performance of servers, and create basic information services. Additionally, students will explore the methods required to secure data and services accessed from the internet to ensure the integrity and confidentiality of critical information.
learning_outcomes: Investigate the layout of server file systems.
Apply technical knowledge to manage servers.
Critically evaluate security policies and procedures.
Plan, create and manage information services.
Design and write scripts to automate various server management tasks.
Justify an appropriate protection strategy for data and services.

title: Literacy Strategies for Learning
school: School of Education
syllabus_overview: Graduate teachers need to know and understand literacy teaching strategies that are particular to their content area and the stage of learning of their students. This subject addresses knowledge and application of those strategies to meet the needs of diverse primary and secondary school classes. It engages with contemporary research-based perspectives and approaches to teaching literacies. The subject also includes application of models and texts to teach numeracy skills to support learning across the curriculum. The subject has a focus on practical strategies for literacy learning and use, especially in relation to written, spoken and visual texts that are subject-specific. Strategies include practices with digital technologies and texts.
learning_outcomes: Teach about texts and their use to inclusively support diverse learners.
Discuss and employ a range of research-based strategies for literacy instruction and assessment.
Discuss and apply subject-specific literacy practices in their teaching areas.
Sequence teaching and learning strategies to scaffold effective literacy development using the multiliteracies pedagogical framework.
Identify and describe digital technologies that can be used for literacy development.
Develop literacy and numeracy instruction for diverse learners that addresses the foci (resources) of the Four Resources Model.

title: Literacy Strategies for Learning

This subject addresses knowledge and application of those strategies to meet the needs of diverse primary and secondary school classes. As part of this, students will engage with contemporary research-based perspectives and approaches to teaching literacies. The subject also includes application of models and texts to teach numeracy skills to support learning across the curriculum. The subject has a focus on practical strategies for literacy learning and use, especially in relation to written, spoken and visual texts that are subject-specific.
