title: Professional Experience and Portfolio
school: School of Information and Communication Studies
syllabus_overview: This subject comprises the supervised workplace experiences within the Master of Education (Teacher Librarianship) course and the completion of the reflective portfolio. The subject will develop an understanding of the nature of professional learning in teacher librarianship and assist students to assemble and analyse evidence of their own learning and professional development through a portfolio approach. Students will then collect and reflect on their learning through selected assignments throughout the course, as well as their study visits and placements. This is the capstone subject of the course, and should be undertaken by students after completing all or most of the other subjects in the course.
learning_outcomes: Engage in dialogue with fellow information professionals.
Have extended expertise in developing a reflective portfolio.
Evaluate the role and functionality of a library or information agency.
Have developed an understanding of common professional goals and practices.
Have a greater understanding of professional learning and reflective practice.
Demonstrate an understanding of the wider library/information community of which school libraries are a part.
Apply theory to practice in a reflective manner.

title: Professional Experience Placement 2
school: School of Nursing, Paramedicine and Healthcare Sciences
syllabus_overview: Students will apply their learning from other Bachelor of Nursing subjects during 160 hours of professional experience placement. The placement is supervised by registered nurses in acute health settings. Students focus on practising safe foundational nursing care including focused, systematic assessments and the administration of medication. Students practice adapting communication to meet the varying health literacy needs of individual people and families.
learning_outcomes: Apply a reflective framework to analyse individual personal and professional experiences and their impact on nursing practice.
Demonstrate respectful communication that recognises the culture, values, beliefs, rights and autonomy of individuals and promotes the integral role of nursing practice in improving health outcomes.
Integrate assessment data and best available evidence to inform person-centred care planning and monitor progress toward expected goals and outcomes.

Demonstrate safe practice by adhering to individual student registered nurse scope of practice and relevant university, profession and industry policies, guidelines, standards, regulations and legislation.

title: Professional Experience Placement 3
school: School of Nursing, Paramedicine and Healthcare Sciences
syllabus_overview: Students will apply their learning from other Bachelor of Nursing subjects during 160 hours of professional experience placement. The placement is supervised by registered nurses in acute health settings. Students apply the procedural skills and techniques required to undertake a broad range of evidence-based and person-centred assessments and interventions. Students develop their ability to evaluate the clinical significance of policies, guidelines and evidence for translation to practice.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse personal and professional experiences and their impact on nursing practice, and identify areas for improvement.
Propose information and resources that empower and support people with their health.

Demonstrate safe practice by adhering to individual student registered nurse scope of practice and relevant university, profession and industry policies, guidelines, standards, regulations and legislation.
Integrate appropriate sources of evidence for safe, quality practice and to monitor progress toward established goals and outcomes.
Demonstrate effective decision making with reference to the ICN Code of Ethics.

title: Professional Experience Placement 4
school: School of Nursing, Paramedicine and Healthcare Sciences
syllabus_overview: Students will apply their learning from other Bachelor of Nursing subjects during a minimum 160 hours of professional experience placement. The placement is supervised by registered nurses. This placement has a specific focus on the mental health and wellbeing of people and health practitioners across health settings. Students demonstrate safe practice at an increasingly independent level and develop skills for coordination of care. Students will actively collaborate with people and health teams as they integrate person-centred assessments and interventions as part of broader, interprofessional plans for care. Students will continue building their professional experience placement portfolio as they critically reflect and plan for future professional experience placements and registered nurse practice.
learning_outcomes: Critically reflect on experiences, knowledge, actions, assumptions, feelings, attitudes and beliefs to comprehensively understand nursing practice and integrate insights into professional development.
Formulate accurate, comprehensive and timely documentation and communication of assessments, plans, actions, monitoring and evaluations.
Develop strategies to support the health and wellbeing of self and others and to maintain capability for practice.

Demonstrate safe practice by adhering to individual student registered nurse scope of practice and relevant university, profession and industry policies, guidelines, standards, regulations and legislation.
Safely delegate tasks to achieve improved health outcomes and coordinate resources effectively and efficiently for planned actions.

title: Professional Experience Placement 5
school: School of Nursing, Paramedicine and Healthcare Sciences
syllabus_overview: Students will apply their learning from other Bachelor of Nursing subjects during a minimum 160 hours of professional experience placement. The placement is supervised by registered nurses in any setting where a registered nurse practices. Students will demonstrate safe practice in accordance with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia (NMBA) Registered Nurse Standards for Practice, Code of Conduct for Nurses and the International Council of Nurses (ICN) Code of Ethics for Nurses. Students will finalise their professional experience placement portfolio and continue their continuing professional development log as they contribute to the professional development of others and critically reflect to support their future as a registered nurse.
learning_outcomes: Collaborate effectively with people, families, communities and health teams to construct and adapt plans for care that include priorities, goals, actions, methods for evaluation, outcomes and timeframes.

Demonstrate safe practice by adhering to individual student registered nurse scope of practice and relevant university, profession and industry policies, guidelines, standards, regulations and legislation.
Critique indivdual nursing practice using an evidence-based reflective framework.
Develop, sustain and conclude effective person centered, therapeutic and professional relationships.
Develop comprehensive, person-centred plans that are safe, appropriate and responsive.

title: Professional Experience Research
school: School of Education
syllabus_overview: This capstone subject is the final subject in the Master of Teaching courses and draws on teacher education students' cumulative learning from across the coursework components of the degree and includes the final professional experience placement. During this professional experience placement students will complete a Teaching Performance Assessment (TPA) in which they will demonstrate they have met the Australian Professional Standards for Teachers (APST) at graduate level. They will also be required to submit evidence of their practice (planning, teaching, assessing and reflecting) and evaluate their impact on school students' learning. Student's satisfactory completion of the TPA is a requirement for graduation from their teacher education program.
learning_outcomes: Reflect on and appraise the impact of their teaching on student outcomes, drawing on relevant theory and evidence collected.
Formulate a plan to address professional learning needs to modify and improve future teaching and progress student learning.
Apply current models of pedagogy and strategies appropriate to the context and stage, to cater for the diverse needs of learners.
Justify (or support) appropriate teaching and learning sequences with student data, including NAPLAN results.

Demonstrate achievement of the Australian Professional Standards for Teachers at graduate level during 30 days of professional experience in a primary classroom setting and satisfactory completion of the TPA.

title: Professional Experience: 3-5 Years
school: School of Education
syllabus_overview: This is the second in a series of professional experience subjects, building on the initial experiences. Students will begin to demonstrate the ability to initiate and sustain positive relationships with individual young children, and guide children's behaviour in positive ways. Students will observe children's play and use these records as a basis for planned experiences. They will reflect on their experiences and adapt their planning in response to feedback and reflection and work collaboratively with their supervising teacher to support children's learning.
learning_outcomes: Use reflective practice in their work with children.
Demonstrate the capacity to create a positive learning environment where children are able to be confident and engaged learners, in alignment with the Early Years Learning Framework (EYLF).
Demonstrate an understanding of, and employ appropriate positive guidance techniques for classroom and behaviour management with 3-5 year old children.
Demonstrate competence in a range of pedagogical, social and administrative skills commensurate with the professional experience setting.
Demonstrate skills of linking child development theory to early childhood practices and programs for 3-5 year old children.

title: Professional Experience: 3-6
school: School of Education
syllabus_overview: This is the third in a series of professional experience subjects, building on students' experience of Primary teaching through a 160 hour supervised placement in a Primary 3-6 setting. Students will apply the theoretical and practical learning outcomes from university based subjects, while under the professional supervision of a practicing classroom teacher. They will develop and apply a range of research informed and contextually appropriate strategies and skills to design, implement, assess and evaluate extended series of context-appropriate lessons in English, Mathematics and other key learning areas. Students will design, implement, assess and evaluate a unit of work for an identified group of learners which will include appropriate pedagogical approaches to meet learners needs.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate effective and contextually appropriate communication skills (questioning, class discussion, interpersonal interaction) that facilitate learning and develop and maintain positive professional relationships.
Identify, evaluate and implement a diverse range of management strategies that are congruent with childrens' learning and behavioural needs and facilitate positive professional relationships.
Apply the process of Backward Design to design a sequence of lessons and/or a unit of work to meet the identified needs of a group of learners.

Critically evaluate significant incidents they experience during their professional experience with reference to current educational theory and in response to formulate and revise personal and professional goals.

To plan and implement differentiated pedagogical and assessment strategies appropriate for a range of diverse learning needs and to form and inform a sequence of lessons appropriate for a group of learners.
prerequisites: EPT217: Professional Experience 3: Primary Classrooms K-2

title: Professional Experience: Birth to 2 years
school: School of Education
syllabus_overview: This subject will assist Pre-Service Teachers (PST's) to acquire an understanding of quality environments for infants and toddlers in early childhood education and care services. The subject incorporates a 120-hour (8hrs/day x 15 days) supervised Work Integrated Learning (WIL) placement where PST's will develop and demonstrate responsive caregiving and education practices that promote the individual capacities of children birth–2 years. The placement will also provide the opportunity for PST's to develop skills in observing, planning, implementing, and reflecting on appropriate experiences for infants and toddlers.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate engagement with each criteria of the Australian Professional Standards for Teachers.

Identify an aspect of improving professional learning, collaborating with colleagues and parents/carers, and abiding by policies and regulations governing the early childhood sector while on placement and discuss how this applies to them.
Begin articulating a narrative around the philosophy of teaching by creating a visual image of a teacher in the E-Portfolio environment.
Identify and reflect on appropriate practice for planning and implementing suitable learning experiences and to create a supportive learning environment for infants and toddlers.

Identify a goal pertaining to the knowledge required for implementing effective teaching and caregiving pedagogy for children birth–2 years and discuss in relation to their professional development as a teacher.

title: Professional Experience: Consolidating Effective Teaching and Assessment in the Primary Years
school: School of Education
syllabus_overview: This capstone subject is the final subject in the Master of Teaching course and draws on teacher education students' cumulative learning from across the coursework components of the degree and includes the final professional experience placement. During this professional experience placement students complete a Teaching Performance Assessment (TPA) in which they demonstrate the Australian Professional Standards for Teachers (APST) at graduate level. They will also be required to submit evidence of their practice (planning, teaching, assessing, reflecting and appraising) through evaluating their impact on school students' learning. In preparation for completing the TPA, students explore the purposes, methods, strengths and challenges of assessing learning in primary school settings. Students examine different approaches, skills and practices for assessing, recording and reporting student's learning. Specific attention is also given to identifying and understanding the challenges and complexities encountered by teachers when assessing and reporting on students' performance and the value of reflection in, on and of practice to improve student learning outcomes. Students' satisfactory completion of a TPA is a requirement to graduate from an accredited teacher education program.
learning_outcomes: Analyse and interpret student assessment data to evaluate student learning and to inform planning and /or to modify subsequent teaching practice to progress student learning.
Apply a range of strategies to assess, record, report and provide feedback to students and parents/carers on achievement of learning outcomes.
Demonstrate achievement of the Australian Professional Standards for Teachers (APST) at graduate level through the satisfactory completion of a Teaching Performance Assessment (TPA).
Plan and justify appropriate teaching and learning sequences with student data, including NAPLAN results.
Formulate a plan to address professional learning needs to modify and improve future teaching and progress student learning.
Reflect on and appraise the impact of their teaching on student outcomes, drawing on relevant theory and evidence collected, to modify and improve future teaching and progress student learning.
Apply current models of pedagogy and strategies appropriate to the context and stage, to cater for the diverse needs of learners.
Use assessment tools and moderation processes to support consistent and comparable, standards based judgements of student learning.
Demonstrate achievement of the Australian Professional Standards for Teachers (APST) at graduate level during 240 hours of professional experience in a primary classroom setting.
prerequisites: EMA410: Teaching and Assessing the Creative Arts
EMS406: Science and Technology Curriculum Studies
EEB505: Indigenous Australian Studies for Teachers

Demonstrate achievement of the Australian Professional Standards for Teachers (APST) at graduate level during 240 hours of professional experience in a secondary classroom setting (Students who completed EPT460 with 200 hours will need to complete EPT449 with 280 hours).
Analyse and interpret student assessment data to evaluate student learning and to inform planning and /or to modify subsequent teaching practice to progress student learning.
Use assessment tools and moderation processes to support consistent and comparable, standards-based judgements of student learning.
Reflect on and appraise the impact of their teaching on student outcomes, drawing on relevant theory and evidence collected, to modify and improve future teaching and progress student learning.
Demonstrate achievement of the Australian Professional Standards for Teachers (APST) at graduate level through the satisfactory completion of a Teaching Performance Assessment (TPA).
prerequisites: EEB435: Indigenous Australian Studies for Teachers
EEP425: Critical Studies in Education and Practice
EPT522: Professional Experience: Consolidating Effective Teaching and Assessment in the Secondary Context

title: Professional Experience: Effective Teaching and Assessment in the Primary Context (3-6)
school: School of Education
syllabus_overview: This capstone subject draws on teacher education students' cumulative learning from across the coursework components of the degree and includes the final professional experience placement for their course. During this professional experience placement, students will complete a Teaching Performance Assessment (TPA) in which they will demonstrate they have met the Australian Professional Standards for Teachers (APST) at a graduate level. They will also be required to submit evidence of their practice (planning, teaching, assessing and reflecting) and evaluate their impact on school students' learning. In preparation for completing the TPA, students will explore the purposes, methods, strengths and challenges of assessing learning in primary school settings. Students will examine different approaches, skills and practices for assessing, recording and reporting children's learning. Specific attention is also given to identifying and understanding the challenges and complexities encountered by teachers when assessing and reporting on students' performance and the value of reflection in, on and of practice to improve student learning outcomes.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate achievement of the Australian Professional Standards for Teachers at graduate level during 240 hours of professional experience in a primary classroom setting.
Use a variety of evidence and data, including NAPLAN results, to plan teaching and learning sequences constructively aligned to curriculum documentation.
Demonstrate achievement of the Australian Professional Standards for Teachers (APST) at a graduate level through the satisfactory completion of a Teaching Performance Assessment (TPA).
Apply a range of strategies to assess, record, report and provide feedback to students and parents/carers on the achievement of learning outcomes.
Reflect on and appraise the impact of their teaching on student outcomes, drawing on relevant theory and evidence collected, to modify and improve future teaching and progress student learning.
Apply current models of pedagogy and strategies appropriate to the context and stage, to cater for the diverse needs of learners.
Use assessment tools and moderation processes to support consistent and comparable, standards-based judgements of student learning.
Analyse and interpret student assessment data to evaluate student learning and to inform planning and /or to modify subsequent teaching practice to progress student learning.

title: Professional Experience: Positive Primary Classroom Environments
school: School of Education
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces students to the role of the teacher in creating positive classroom environments for a range of diverse learners through online study with a classroom experience focus. The professional experience component consists of up to a 200 hour placement in a Primary K-2 or 3-6 setting. Students will apply their learning from the online modules while under the professional supervision of a practicing classroom teacher. They will develop and apply their knowledge of a range of appropriate classroom management strategies to their professional practice as they design, implement and evaluate context appropriate lessons in key learning areas. They will apply strategies that promote positive relationships within the classroom, as well as beginning to apply strategies to manage student behaviour. Students will also provide evidence of their progression in developing competence across the Australian Professional Standards for Teachers (APST) at a Graduate level.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate current educational theory, policy and personal experiences to formulate and revise professional teaching goals prior to, during and after professional experience.
Apply a clear knowledge of the legal and practical requirements designed to ensure student and teacher safety in the classroom.

Describe and evaluate positive school and classroom environments with reference to physical, social, cultural, emotional, and intellectual development, and explain their implications for learning and behaviour.
Plan, implement and critically evaluate a variety of classroom management strategies to inform a sequence of lessons appropriate for a range of diverse learning needs.
Apply and reflect on theoretical models to create effective learning environments and interpersonal relationships with children, parents/care givers and communities.
Research, implement and evaluate proactive and reactive strategies that inform classroom management plans.
prerequisites: EPT447: Professional Experience: Positive Primary Classroom Environments

title: Professional Experience: Positive Primary Classroom Environments

Critically evaluate current educational theory, policy and personal experiences to formulate and revise professional teaching goals prior to, during and after professional experience.
Identify, apply and reflect on theoretical models to create effective learning environments and interpersonal relationships with children, parents/care givers and communities.
Plan and implement a variety of classroom management strategies to inform a sequence of lessons appropriate for a range of diverse learning needs.
Design and implement proactive and reactive strategies that inform classroom management plans.
prerequisites: EPT510: Professional Experience: Positive Primary Classroom Environments

title: Professional Experience: Teacher as Professional in the Secondary Context
school: School of Education
syllabus_overview: This subject draws together teacher education students' discipline-specific pedagogical content knowledge and skills in preparation for, and during, a 240 hour professional experience placement in a secondary school setting. Students will analyse and reflect on the quality of their teaching in previous placements and explore how to improve aspects of their teaching practice. Students will use the Quality Teaching Model and the Graduate Teaching Standards to frame their reflection and dialogue, and to set learning goals for improving teaching and learning. In collaboration with their supervising teachers, students will plan, teach, assess and reflect on learning as appropriate to their classes and in alignment with secondary curriculum requirements. Students will collaborate with members of the wider school community and develop strategies to recognise the diversity and differences amongst learners. Students will provide evidence of their commitment to, and progression toward attaining the Australian Professional Standards for Teachers at the graduate level.
learning_outcomes: Reflect on teaching practices, identify learning goals, and engage in professional dialogue with members of the profession and the wider school community for improving teaching and learning.
Discuss and use various typologies of quality teaching to reflect on, evaluate and improve aspects of their teaching practice.
Explore positionality through reflection and reflexive practice as students and educators.
Critique a range of assessment strategies and moderation activities appropriate to the context.
Apply current models of teaching and learning for a range of learners across a range of year levels (7-12).
Describe aspects of diversity and strategies to recognise the diversity and differences amongst a class of learners.

Apply sociological understandings of social justice issues relevant to gender, ethnicity, social class, and religion in planning for and teaching diverse learners across a range of year levels (7-12).
Submit a professional experience placement report demonstrating the successful completion of a 240 hour professional experience placement in a secondary school.
Demonstrate an applied knowledge of, and provide evidence of growth as a teaching professional in relation to, the Australian Professional Standards for Teachers.

title: Professional Fundamentals
school: School of Dentistry and Medical Sciences
syllabus_overview: The student's journey to become a health practitioner begins with this subject. Students explore the principles of professionalism and professional practice through a structured introduction to the practical aspects of the clinical environment. The subject considers theory and skill development in communication, cultural safety, ethical practice and patient care. A multi-disciplinary approach is undertaken through inclusion of historical and current imaging practices in diagnostic radiography, nuclear medicine and radiation therapy. The chest x-ray, bone scan and fundamentals of radiation therapy will be studied.
learning_outcomes: Explain and apply the legal, ethical, professional, and regulatory responsibilities of a medical radiation science practitioner, including the use of correct professional terminology, and appropriate professional behaviour (MRPBA Domain 2.1 and 2.3).
Identify and describe the role of patient advocacy in medical radiation science and the potential barriers to effective patient communication (MRPBA Domain 2.4 and 3.1).
Recognise and describe the process for reviewing a patient history, referral requirements and confirming appropriateness of the procedure (MRPBA Domain 1.2c and 1.4).

Recognise and describe appropriate procedures and processes to ensure safe patient management, and legal responsibilities with respect to health, safety and hazards in the workplace (MRPBA Domain 5.2 and 5.4).

title: Professional Issues in Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Mental Health
school: School of Nursing, Paramedicine and Healthcare Sciences
syllabus_overview: This subject explores current issues within the mental health landscape that may contribute to professional resilience, including increasing individual capacities to address professional burnout and support the development of personal stress management plans. Students will learn how to identify signs of personal stress and gain an understanding of where resources may be available to assist them in addressing personal and professional issues within the workplace and in their everyday lives. Contemporary professional issues in Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander mental health practice will be examined including areas of competency development, evidence-based practice, employment trends and workplace environments.
learning_outcomes: Examine and articulate the difference between the role of the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander mental health professionals and other mental health professionals, and critically examine their role in a multidisciplinary team.
Identify and plan for professional issues impacting on Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander mental health workers.
Identify and discuss current issues in the field of mental health that influence professional practice.
Critically reflect on personal strengths, skills and achievements as they relate to the mental health profession.
Identify warning signs of stress and burnout and discuss a personal stress management plan.
Select and utilise appropriate resources relevant to professional practice.

title: Professional Internship
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Computing, Mathematics and Engineering
syllabus_overview: This is a supervised internship subject. Students who have completed 16 credit points of study will be able to apply for enrolment. Within this subject, students will spend approximately 105 hours during the session working on a project or activity in a private or public sector organisation under the guidance of an industry mentor. Additionally students will spend time on study such as reflecting on the placement. Students will gain experience of the Australian workplace culture and environment while being involved in a range of activities in fields such as IT, Digital Marketing, or Project Management. Students will be individually placed with suitable organisations and the type of work experience will vary.
learning_outcomes: Complete a supervised internship relevant to a student's academic study program.
Apply business skills and workplace competencies.
Critically evaluate and apply conceptual and theoretical knowledge to a specific workplace environment.
Appraise their personal development across a range of professional practice skills.

title: Professional Learning and Networking
school: School of Information and Communication Studies
syllabus_overview: This subject focusses on the development of students' professional capabilities relevant to being a reflective information professional. They explore professional identity and the importance of continuing professional development as an essential component of professional practice. They participate and reflect on professional learning activities relevant to developing their own knowledge, skills and attributes as an information professional. Students engage in practical activities such as building their professional portfolio, networks and career planning.
learning_outcomes: Reflect on what it means to be an information professional.
Effectively engage in professional networking and career planning activities.
Reflect on and document participation in professional development activities.
Articulate the value of continuing professional development to reflective, professional practice and lifelong learning.

title: Professional Legal Conduct
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: Centre for Law & Justice
syllabus_overview: This subject examines critically the nature of the legal profession and its role in society. In particular, it introduces students to skills of ethical problem solving within the context of professional practice, and the regulations and standards that govern them. A significant component of the subject covers discrete problems of legal ethics such as confidentiality, access to justice, truth in the adversarial system, conflicts of interest and relationships between lawyers, clients and the community. Students are also introduced to the principles of trust accounting.
learning_outcomes: Present a clear, coherent and independent exposition of the way the legal profession's conduct is regulated in Australia (particularly NSW), including disciplinary processes, apparatus and functions.

Act autonomously to present a clear and coherent exposition of knowledge that manifests professional judgement to questions relating to breaches of professional accountability, including the ramifications of breach of trust.
Critically engage with the principles of trust accounting, including identifying and solving problems within the lawyer-client context.

Identify and analyse value conflicts and ethical dilemmas that occur in professional legal practice and propose solutions by applying legal, statutory and ethical principles to hypothetical scenarios to resolve those issues.
Critically analyse the role of the lawyer within the context of the Australian adversarial system, including the cost of justice and alternatives to litigation.

Critically analyse statutory, common law and other legal mechanisms of accountability including obligations to the client, court, practitioners and others and reflect upon philosophical theories and social justice policies underpinning this area of the law.

Use initiative and judgement to analyse critically persuasive legal argument that applies the relevant regulation and theoretical insights to both practical issues and theoretical understandings pertaining to the role of the modern-day lawyer.
Demonstrate an in-depth understanding of the values, principles and standards of practice articulated in the professional codes of ethics and the provision of relevant statutes and case law.

title: Professional Nursing: Evidence-informed Practice
school: School of Nursing, Paramedicine and Healthcare Sciences
syllabus_overview: Students undertaking this subject will develop their capacity to appreciate the importance of nursing and midwifery research to inform practice and health care. The significance of being able to appraise research and apply it to practice is highlighted. This subject focuses on developing a fundamental understanding of the research process, research designs, and major data collection and analytical methods. Skills necessary to understand published research are introduced. It includes ethical and cultural considerations to research, how to critique the literature and how to inform and change practice based on evidence.
learning_outcomes: Apply the principles of ethical research and cultural competence in critically appraising research articles (NMBA 1.3, 2.1, 2.3, 3.1, 9.3, 9.5).
Critically evaluate research articles and their applicability to nursing practice (NMBA 2.2, 2.4, 2.5, 2.6, 3.1, 3.4, 3.5, 4.1, 5.1, 7.3, 9.4, 9.5, 10.2, 10.4).
Describe the research process and explain its components (NMBA 4.1, 7.3, 10.4).

Evaluate the relationships between research, theory and evidence-based practice for nursing (aligns with Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia National Competency Standards for the Registered Nurse: 2.6, 3.4, 9.2).
prerequisites: NRS193: Discipline of Nursing 1: Contexts of Nursing
NRS313: Professional Nursing: Transition to Practice

title: Professional Paramedic Practice
school: School of Nursing, Paramedicine and Healthcare Sciences
syllabus_overview: This subject prepares students for paramedic practice by advancing autonomous clinical judgment, evidence-based decision-making, and culturally safe, person-centred care focussing on diverse populations, including First Nations people. Learning is facilitated through community-based simulations that replicate real-world paramedicine practice environments and are supported by online resources. During these authentic simulations, students will apply clinical practice guidelines in structured scenarios, conducting assessments and developing tailored treatment plans. During simulations, students are provided opportunities to engage with the legal, ethical, and regulatory frameworks of contemporary paramedicine. Additionally, students will refine essential professional capabilities, adhere to codes of conduct set by regulatory bodies like the Paramedicine Board of Australia, and develop effective communication, collaboration, and self-reflection skills to identify and address skill gaps.
learning_outcomes: Apply clinical knowledge and skills, and decision-making in diverse environments that replicate real-world paramedic settings under supervision.
Apply principles of person-centred care to address factors which underpin the health and social status of people accessing paramedic care.
Identify and evaluate the appropriateness and real impact of treatment plans tailored to the individual, providing culturally safe care to First Nations people and other diverse populations.
Reflect on their professional skills and knowledge to identify areas for improvement and develop sustainable strategies for continuous professional development.
Engage in professional communication, collaboration and leadership with other health professionals, agencies, health consumers and society.
prerequisites: PAR100: Foundations of Clinical Paramedic Practice
PAR103: Introduction to Contemporary Paramedic Practice

title: Professional Nursing: Transition to Practice
school: School of Nursing, Paramedicine and Healthcare Sciences
syllabus_overview: This subject will examine a broad range of contemporary issues and trends that impact on nurses and nursing within the Australian health care context, such as risk management, patient safety, clinical governance, scope of practice, with an emphasis on the importance of professional communication, leadership and management. The focus of this subject is to prepare the graduating nurse with the necessary skills to transition from a nursing student into a registered nurse who is industry ready. This includes preparing the student for professional registration and professional interviews. It will ensure the student is equipped with the appropriate tools such as an e-portfolio, and interview skills to successfully transition.
learning_outcomes: Present an e-portfolio which meets NMBA standards of maintaining a record of involvement in both formal and informal professional development (NMBA 1.1, 2.1).

Describe and explain the nurses' scope of practice, including legal obligations and constraints (aligns with Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia National Competency Standards for the Registered Nurse: 1.1, 1.2, 2.1, 2.2, 2.5, 8.1, 8.2).
Use the principles of clinical governance and quality improvement to undertake a root cause analysis related to nursing practice (NMBA 1.3, 2.2, 2.4, 3.3, 3.4, 3.5, 4.1, 7.4, 7.8, 8.1, 10.4).
Critically analyse incidents involving patient safety and make appropriate recommendations(NMBA 1.2, 2.1, 2.2, 2.5, 3.2, 6.4, 9.1, 9.2, 10.2, 10.3).

Demonstrate leadership and management strategies by providing recommendations for changes in health care practice to address quality issues (NMBA 1.3, 2.2, 2.4, 2.5, 3.5, 7.4, 7.5, 7.6, 9.2, 10.2, 10.3, 10.4).
prerequisites: NRS223: Essential Nursing Care: Chronic and Complex Nursing
NRS123: Professional Nursing: Health Law for Nurses

title: Professional Pharmacy Practice
school: School of Dentistry and Medical Sciences
syllabus_overview: This subject falls within the pharmacy discipline known as Pharmacy Practice which is defined by the World Health Organisation (WHO) and peak pharmacy bodies within Australia and globally as being concerned with the roles of pharmacists, including expanding and developing roles, and the skills, knowledge and behaviours consistent with those roles. Professional Pharmacy Practice provides learning opportunities for development of the necessary skills and abilities required of all practising pharmacists in Australia and for the development of the appropriate professional identity and philosophy. Chronic disease management and professional practice initiatives are key content in this subject. Students studying this subject are assumed to have completed the first three years of the standard enrolment pattern as this knowledge is a critical success factor in achieving professional milestones which are necessary to pass this subject.
learning_outcomes: Research and review complementary medicines for patient utility and safety.
Demonstrate ability to analyse the practice environment to ethically incorporate appropriate complementary medicines into patient disease management.
Identify, analyse and work effectively to solve practice-relevant issues.
Practise legally and to accepted standards.
Constructively collaborate with others and manage conflict.
Participate in and develop processes to provide a safe and secure workplace by managing pharmacy resources.
Review patient documentation for safety and appropriateness and supply medicines accordingly.
Deliver quality and safe patient-centred care to the standard required of a graduate.
Reflect on the role, practice and professional identity of the pharmacist to develop and maintain competence for current and future practice.
Engage in the self-directed evaluation of information and issues from various sources and articulate the decision-making process.
Research, critically analyse and synthesise information appropriate for the audience.
Deliver primary and preventative health care to the standard required of a graduate.
Communicate effectively and professionally with stakeholders and deliver considered and clear professional decisions, information or opinions.

title: Professional Placement
school: School of Information and Communication Studies
syllabus_overview: This workplace learning subject builds on INF571 Planning for Professional Placement. In this subject students will undertake the 80 hour professional placement approved in INF571. Students will gain a deeper understanding of information organisations and apply theoretical skills and knowledge. The placement is aligned with the student's career goals and professional expectations/standards. Students will demonstrate an ability to effectively engage in and reflect on real-life working environments. This subject is the second of two Professional Placement subjects. In this subject students will undertake their professional placement and write a reflective report.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate effective engagement in an information workplace setting.
Analyse and apply relevant theories to practical situations.
Critically reflect on, and articulate, their workplace learning experiences.
Contextualise and evaluate an information workplace and the role and function in the community it serves.
Successfully complete a minimum 80 hour placement in a role that meets the professional standards required by accrediting bodies.

title: Professional Placement
school: School of Information and Communication Studies
syllabus_overview: This workplace learning subject builds on INF221 Planning for Professional Placement. In this subject students will undertake the professional placement approved in INF221. Students will gain a deeper understanding of information organisations and apply theoretical skills and knowledge. The placement is aligned with the student's career goals and professional expectations/standards. Students will demonstrate an ability to effectively engage in and reflect on real-life working environments. This subject is the second of two Professional Placement subjects. In this subject students will undertake their professional placement and write a reflective report.
learning_outcomes: Provide an overview of an information workplace and the role and function in the community it serves.
Identify and apply relevant theories to practical situations.
Demonstrate effective engagement in an information workplace setting.
Reflect on and articulate their workplace learning experiences.
Successfully complete a minimum 80 hour placement in a role that meets the professional standards required by accrediting bodies.

title: Professional Practice
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Business
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces students to the world of the business professional. Students will learn the basic tools used in professional business practice and develop industry connections through an immersive learning approach. The subject will focus on building practical skills that are used in business and connect students to their real world application through the inclusion of business professionals in the delivery of the subject. The curriculum of the subject will be closely aligned to industry developments and best practice.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate proficiency in spreadsheet and other data presentation software.
Analyse basic data and communicate the findings in both written and verbal presentations to a management audience.
Understand the use and relevance of social media for business marketing and stakeholder engagement.
Demonstrate proficiency in current business tools such as Google docs, Dropbox etc.
Understand and evaluate the needs and drivers of regional businesses.

title: Professional Practice
school: School of Agricultural, Environmental and Veterinary Sciences
syllabus_overview: This subject allows students to experience first-hand the requirements of working in industry and to develop a realistic understanding of the expectations placed upon workers within legal and practical contexts. During this subject important factors that shape the equine industry will be evaluated and their effect on industry practice appraised. This subject includes reflection and assessment of the (required) extramural workplace learning that students have undertaken. On successful completion of this subject students will have engaged in personal career goal setting and produced a personal development plan, that will be met in part through working within the equine industry.
learning_outcomes: Develop and demonstrate effective autonomous and team working skills.
Justify their own and the behaviour of others in terms of industry ethics in relation to horse welfare and human safety.
Assemble a workplace learning and professional development portfolio to an appropriate professional standard showing development, progression and reflective evaluation throughout.
Problem solve within the industry context in the light of limitations and opportunities including Indigenous competency and as custodians of the environment.
Tailor communications to different audiences as appropriate.
Identify and critically appraise personal and professional skills and career goals.

title: Professional Practice
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Business
syllabus_overview: This subject broadly introduces students to the accounting profession, financial accounting, management accounting, ethics and professional codes of conduct with a focus on professional competencies required in practice. Throughout the subject, students will explore and develop a range of critical interpersonal, communication and personal skills that have been identified by professional accounting bodies.
learning_outcomes: Discuss key aspects of the business environment, how technology has impacted businesses, and technological advances that support data analysis, decision making, and enhances the efficiency and effectiveness of communication.
Deliver engaging presentations that persuade, motivate and inform stakeholders using a range of technologies and presentation strategies.
Discuss personal skills that are essential when working individually and collaboratively in the workplace, and evaluate personal strengths and areas that require further development.
Explain the importance accounting professional and ethical standards and apply ethical principles to a range of business situations.
Evaluate data and information from a variety of sources and apply critical thinking skills to identify and solve problems and make business decisions.
Communicate clearly and concisely in a range of formal and informal situations and settings.
Apply negotiation and conflict resolution management principles in a range of business settings.

title: Professional Practice in Accounting
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Business
syllabus_overview: In this subject students will explore a range of employability skills which will enhance their future transition to professional life and assist in career planning. Students will, in conjunction with the subject co-ordinator, select one of two streams of work-related activity: a new project at their usual place of employment; or a work placement at a host organisation. These streams will provide opportunities for students to consider the professional skills needed within a work environment and to develop the employability skills needed for future career progression.
learning_outcomes: Learn and assess through reflection.
Prepare an effective job application.
Define, evaluate, and reflect on employability skills and graduate attributes to plan appropriate professional development activities.
Explore and enhance personal brand development through academic application and self-development.
Reflect effectively on working conditions and activities that had been undertaken during a work placement.
Explore, develop and evaluate a personal career plan.
prerequisites: ACC276: Work Integrated Learning in Accounting

title: Professional Practice in Education and Training
school: School of Education
syllabus_overview: Students will be able to formulate professional planning goals to consider how technology can be adopted to enhance aspects of a workplace. Students will spend one semester working on a technology training project evaluating the learning processes with a view to enhance an existing or future workplace context. The potential of applying a selected technology into the workplace will be reflected upon in light of theory, scholarship and professional practices. The type of technology training project will vary, with students in an existing workplace able to trial and evaluate a selected technology for implementation in their own context under the guidance of a workplace mentor. Students without an existing workplace context are required to undertake an analysis of a training program in a selected technology to enhance the skills, knowledge and professional practice that will be required for application to a future workplace context. Students who have completed at least 32 credit points of their Masters degree can enter EEB506: Professional Practice in Education and Training.
learning_outcomes: Formulate personal professional planning goals through the consideration of how a technology can be authentically used, developed and integrated to enhance aspects of a workplace.
Evaluate technology training processes to develop skills, knowledge and professional practice for application to existing or future workplace contexts.
Reflect critically on theory, scholarship and professional practice to evaluate the potential of applying selected technologies into the workplace.
Analyse training situations in which a selected technology might be implemented and utilised in authentic, innovative or flexible ways.

title: Professional Practice in Geospatial Science
school: School of Agricultural, Environmental and Veterinary Sciences
syllabus_overview: This subject integrates academic learning with practical experience, equipping students for the geospatial science workforce through authentic and engaging Work Integrated Learning (WIL) opportunities. Students will critically and creatively address real-world challenges, integrating knowledge from prior studies to develop innovative and effective solutions based on the application of geospatial science. By combining problem-based learning with reflective practice, this subject deepens understanding of professional practice in geospatial science while fostering professional identity, knowledge, and workplace skills. Through meaningful workplace learning experiences—whether via a new host organisation, advanced projects within their current roles, or tailored projects and professional certifications related to the course learning outcomes—students will enhance their professional development, critical reflective practice, and work ethic. This subject provides an opportunity for students to consolidate their academic and practical expertise, preparing them as competent geospatial professionals while able to advance knowledge through meaningful practical contributions to the geospatial science discipline.
learning_outcomes: Apply geospatial and AI tools ethically and sustainably to inform workplace decisions and enhance solutions, addressing challenges such as data privacy, bias, and societal impacts.
Critically evaluate workplace experiences to identify growth opportunities, refine career goals, and strengthen professional identity within the geospatial science field.
Independently complete workplace or project-based tasks using geospatial tools, methods and knowledge to address specific challenge.
Demonstrate professional skills in communication, teamwork, and technical competencies through participation in authentic work integrated learning experiences.
Critically analyse and solve practical problems by integrating academic and workplace knowledge.

title: Professional Programming Practice
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Computing, Mathematics and Engineering
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces students to aspects of professional programming practice related to the production and debugging of quality software. It addresses the basic principles of teamwork and the issues surrounding online teams including the application of version control and testing techniques.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse software programs and apply theories of debugging together with specialised and technical skills to generate solutions to complex debugging problems.
Identify the purpose and limitations of software testing.
Demonstrate the ability to work effectively in a team environment.
Design and implement an appropriate suite of software tests to support the complete system development life cycle.
Recognise and apply knowledge and skills to effectively utilize version control as part of professional programming practice.

title: Professional Psychology Placement 1
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Psychology
syllabus_overview: This is the first of two 150 hour placements which students are required to undertake in an area of professional psychology practice and complete an empirical single-case report, based on one clinical condition (e.g., Major Depressive Disorder) encountered during the placement
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate applied knowledge of theories of psychopathology.
Demonstrate proficiency in applied psychological assessment.
Conduct practice in accordance with professional and ethical standards.
Demonstrate competence in adopting an evidence - based approach to psychological practice through completion of an experimental single case report.
Demonstrate proficiency in the delivery of evidence-based psychological interventions, and the conduct of appropriate evaluation of outcome.
Demonstrate proficiency in diagnosis and case formulation.

title: Professional Psychology Placement 2
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Psychology
syllabus_overview: This is the second of two 150 hour placements which students are required to undertake in an area of professional psychology practice and complete an empirical case report detailing the psychological work undertaken.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate satisfactory performance on supervisor evaluation.
Design and implement psychotherapeutic interventions for clients with a range of complex and comorbid psychological conditions.
Conduct practice in accordance with professional and ethical standards.
Recognise the impact of socio-cultural factors and modify interventions appropriately.

Reflect on the theoretical implications of treatment outcomes relative to case presentation/formulation, and thus evaluate implications for theories of psychopathology of treatment success, and consider potential implications of treatment failures on both theory and practice.

title: Professional Study Visit (4 points)
school: School of Information and Communication Studies
syllabus_overview: This subject will expose students to a range of information agencies to develop a deeper understanding of both the career opportunities available within the profession, and how various information agencies function to service a particular clientele.
learning_outcomes: Discuss the range and variety of information agencies and the services they offer.
Describe the operation of a range of information agencies and the interaction of the agencies with their users.
Reflect upon how theoretical and technical knowledge is applied in the workplace.
Describe the role of the information professional in various contexts.

title: Professional Study Visit (PG) (4)
school: School of Information and Communication Studies
syllabus_overview: This subject will expose students to a range of information agencies to develop a deeper understanding of both the career opportunities available within the profession, and how various information agencies function to service a particular clientele.
learning_outcomes: Critically reflect upon how theoretical and technical knowledge is applied within workplaces.
Critically evaluate the operation of a range of information agencies and how these interact with their users.
Compare the range and variety of information agencies and the services they offer, with consideration of frameworks, standards and professional practice.

title: Professional Study Visit in Animal, Equine and Veterinary Sciences
school: Centre of Veterinary Sciences
syllabus_overview: This subject is designed to give students first hand experience of a range of clinical or research activities within the Centre of Veterinary Sciences. It is designed to allow national and international external students to undertake up to nine weeks training within the school.
learning_outcomes: Have developed a sound knowledge and practical skills in specific areas of animal science, equine science, veterinary science, clinical practice and or research.

title: Professional Supervision 1
school: School of Theology
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces students to the key aspects of professional supervision. The students will learn advanced skills and knowledge in a range of areas, including how to establish and manage a supervision relationship, how to facilitate transformational learning for a supervisee, how to provide professional supervision in a range of contexts, how to distinguish professional supervision from other forms of reflective practice, how to undertake professional and theological reflection, and how to apply legal and ethical responsibilities within professional and ministry contexts.
learning_outcomes: Articulate a personal ethical approach for their own practice, including an ability to recognise and competently address the wide range of ethical and legal concerns in supervision.
Establish and manage a contracted and confidential supervision relationship through use of advanced skills in creating rapport and demonstrating empathy.

Demonstrate advanced skills in the selection of and use of supervision techniques from a wide range of professional supervision theories and models, demonstrating sensitivity, creativity and flexibility in their approach.
Critically evaluate ethical issues arising in professional supervision, demonstrating knowledge of ethical and theological approaches to these issues.
Demonstrate facilitation of transformational learning through use of advanced communication, goal setting and evaluation skills.
Critically reflect on key issues arising in professional supervision using rigorous, intentional theological reflection.
Critically differentiate between professional supervision and other professional development practices including, mentoring, coaching, pastoral care and spiritual direction.
Critically reflect on their own personal process as a professional supervisor.

title: Professional Supervision 2
school: School of Theology
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces students to the key aspects of professional supervision in both clinical and pastoral contexts. The students will learn advanced skills and knowledge in a range of areas, including how to establish and manage a supervision relationship; how to provide professional supervision in ministry, community sector, and professional contexts; how to undertake professional reflection; how to plan group interventions; how to provide ethical and pastoral advice; and how to apply legal and ethical responsibilities within professional and ministry contexts.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate advanced knowledge and skills in professional supervision within a ministry or professional context.

Demonstrate an in-depth understanding of the importance of a professional supervision methodology as a critical and constructive enterprise for reflective practice in ministry and professional contexts.
Demonstrate knowledge of legal principles and obligations applicable to professional supervision in ministry and professional contexts.
Demonstrate advanced communication skills to justify and interpret professional decisions to religious practitioners and laity.
Demonstrate high-level personal autonomy and accountability in the execution of professional supervision.

Demonstrate a critical understanding of ethical approaches to professional supervision in ministry or professional contexts and articulate a personal ethical approach for the professional implementation of their own practice.

title: Professional Systems Security
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Computing, Mathematics and Engineering
syllabus_overview: In this subject students will analyse and apply content from the eight domains that comprise a Common Body of Knowledge (CBK) for information systems security professionals. This subject will also help students prepare for the Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP) industry certification exam from the International Information Systems Security Certification Consortium (ISC²).
learning_outcomes: Formulate a security management policy.
Select appropriate industry frameworks and regulations to support security analysis and recommendations.
Justify key elements of operations security.
Apply structured threat and risk assessments to analyse an enterprise environment.
Compare and select appropriate secure system architectures.
Describe common application security threats and justify appropriate security countermeasures.

title: Professionalism and Resilience in Public Safety and Security
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: Australian Graduate School of Policing Security
syllabus_overview: This subject examines the meaning of professionalism in the domain of public safety. Public safety employees will typically have roles serving their communities in the police, paramedicine, nursing, social work and other related fields. Public expectations for the quality and sustainability of services provided by their public safety professionals are high. Students undertaking this subject who aspire to work in the public safety sector will explore the meaning of professionalism, and what it means to be a professional. There are many difficult challenges in working in public safety; challenges to organisations as well as to individual employees. In this subject, the concept of resilience, and being resilient will be explored. Students will reflect on their own personal motivation for pursuing a public safety career, and will examine strategies to build their personal resilience, their emotional intelligence and their personal and professional competence. This subject will explore a range of issues relating to professionalism and resilience in public safety, and will utilise case studies and reflective practice as a tool for developing learning.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate a knowledge and understanding of the role of resilience in personal, organisational and public contexts/settings.
Demonstrate an understanding of the importance of equality, diversity and cultural competence in the delivery of public safety and security services/public services.

Critically anlayse the relationships between themselves, their colleagues, their organisation, their profession and other service agencies, and the role of these relationships in maintaining public safety and security.
Apply the principles of reflective practice at personal, professional and organisational levels through the completion of a personal development action plan.
Demonstrate a knowledge of their chosen profession, professional ethical codes of practice; and what it means to be a 'professional'.

Demonstrate the literacy, research and communication skills necessary to identify, understand, interpret and use/apply relevant information from a range of sources, and communicate these effectively and respectfully according to the context, including in interactions with academic staff and students and in assessment tasks.

title: Professionals Skills in Criminology
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: Centre for Law & Justice
syllabus_overview: The Professionals Skills in Criminology subject focuses upon identification and development of student academic and professional skills for successful degree completion and future employment. Students will review their experience in the first session, identify and articulate skills strengths and gaps and strategies for academic success. The subject links these strategies and skills development to career aspirations, with creation of key documents and a portfolio of student work. Skills development will include a focus upon research, analysis, communication, conflict management, mediation, and cultural competency. Students will be able to identify, articulate and demonstrate an understanding of the nexus between academic and professional skills, and employer expectations.
learning_outcomes: be able to identify and articulate their academic knowledge and skills in the context of career pathways;
be able to prepare key documents (e.g. curriculum vitae) for future employment.
be able to demonstrate literacy and numeracy skills appropriate for criminal justice practice;
be able to identify and develop their individual skills;
be able to identify key strategies and pathways to a preferred career; and
be able to understand and articulate academic and professional skills;

title: Programming Principles
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Computing, Mathematics and Engineering
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces students to the principles of programming. It begins with the development of problem solving skills relevant to the solution of programming problems. This subject is one of the foundation subjects for other studies in Information Technology because it develops skills, techniques and approaches that underpin many other areas of the computing discipline.
learning_outcomes: Interpret algorithms and program code.
Apply sound program analysis, design, coding, debugging, testing and documentation techniques for simple programming problems.
Identify, isolate and correct errors in all phases of the programming process.
Explain the steps involved in a disciplined approach to problem-solving, algorithm development and coding.
Write code in an appropriate coding language.
Demonstrate and explain elements of good programming style.

title: Programming for Students with High Support Needs
school: School of Education
syllabus_overview: This subject will examine the development of curriculum for students who have complex disabilities and a high level of support need. The focus is on the overall process of curriculum development from functional curriculum based assessments to the decisions of what, how and when to teach. Development of specific Individual Educational Programmes will be emphasised across learning domains.
learning_outcomes: Select instructional pedagogies and strategies suited to prioritised skills.
Conduct functional assessments across all relevant curriculum domains.
Engage in collaborative consultation and problem solving with all stakeholders to make informed decisions for learners.
Integrate technology (ICT) across skills within adaptive behaviour curriculum areas.
Analyse standardised assessment instruments and translate results into programming objectives.
Cater for the needs of learners with complex and multiple disabilities.
Make decisions about appropriate modes of communication including augmentative and alternative systems (AAC) as determined by need.
Make informed decisions about assessment, planning, implementation and evaluation of IEPs.

title: Program and Portfolio Management
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Business
syllabus_overview: Program management encompasses the coordinated management of multiple projects designed to implement strategies and deliver specific benefits. Portfolio management encompasses those programs and projects needed to achieve strategic business objectives. This subject gives students the skills and understanding required for coordinated management of multiple projects directed toward strategic business and organisational objectives. Students will learn the Project Management Institute (PMI®) processes for both program and portfolio management and will be able to apply them in the correct context and situation.
learning_outcomes: Justify how risk and communication management relates to strategic business goals.
Understand and apply the principles of program and portfolio management to the realisation of benefits for an organisation.
Design portfolio and program plans to bring about strategic business change.
Explain and defend the value of program and portfolio management for large organisations.
Implement and justify the PMI® processes and methods for program and portfolio management.
Differentiate and compare program, portfolio and project management concepts and principles.

title: Programming in GIS and Remote Sensing
school: School of Agricultural, Environmental and Veterinary Sciences
syllabus_overview: In this subject spatial scientists are introduced to solving complex spatial problems using programming techniques. Two open source programming languages, R and Python, are introduced to develop a life-long learning capability in spatial programming. Open source spatial analysis software is also explored to provide the student with a more comprehensive spatial science toolbox than is provided by popular commercial GIS and remote sensing software applications. Programming techniques are demonstrated by solving selected spatial modelling problems. Intermediate level knowledge of geographic information science is assumed. Students who complete this subject will have advanced skills in programming techniques to solve a spatial modelling problem.
learning_outcomes: Utilise open source spatial software to carry out spatial analysis and modelling.
Describe and compare open source spatial software.
Apply programming skills to provide spatial analysis solutions.
Design, construct and implement programming techniques to solve a spatial modelling problem.

title: Programming in Java
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Computing, Mathematics and Engineering
syllabus_overview: This subject covers problem-solving, computer program design and implementation in Java at an introductory level. Programming concepts are presented using an object-oriented approach and students learn how to develop programs using object-oriented techniques. The subject covers class design, the use of inheritance in class design and the use of aggregation techniques. Students learn to develop small applications consisting of a number of classes.
learning_outcomes: Implement basic algorithms in Java.
Use object-oriented techniques and Java resources to develop small applications consisting of a number of classes.
Apply inheritance and aggregation patterns in the design and implementation of programs.
Manipulate simple file operations using Java.
Interpret design requirements expressed in UML (Unified Modelling Language).
Apply basic testing and debugging techniques in program development.

title: Programming in Java 1
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Computing, Mathematics and Engineering
syllabus_overview: This subject covers problem-solving, computer program design, implementation and evaluation in Java. Students learn to develop object-oriented applications consisting of a number of classes. The object-oriented approach is compared with other programming paradigms. The subject covers class design, file manipulation, Graphical User Interface components, and the use of inheritance and aggregation techniques.
learning_outcomes: Manipulate file operations through Java programming.
Apply inheritance and aggregation patterns in the design and implementation of programs.
Interpret and evaluate design requirements expressed in Unified Modelling Language (UML).
Design and implement algorithms in Java.
Use object-oriented techniques and Java resources to develop small applications consisting of a number of classes.
Implement Graphical User Interface (GUI) components using Java.
Apply testing and debugging techniques in program development.
Compare and critically evaluate different programming paradigms.

title: Programming in Java 1
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Computing, Mathematics and Engineering
syllabus_overview: This subject covers problem-solving, computer program design and implementation in Java at an introductory level. Programming concepts are presented using an object-oriented approach and students learn how to develop programs using object-oriented techniques. The subject covers class design, the use of inheritance in class design and the use of aggregation techniques. Students learn to develop small applications consisting of a number of classes.
learning_outcomes: Implement basic algorithms in Java.
Apply inheritance and aggregation patterns in the design and implementation of programs.
Interpret design requirements expressed in UML (Unified Modelling Language).
Use object-oriented techniques and Java resources to develop small applications consisting of a number of classes.
Manipulate simple file operations using Java.
Apply basic testing and debugging techniques in program development.

title: Programming in Java 2
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Computing, Mathematics and Engineering
syllabus_overview: This subject teaches students to apply and analyse advanced object-oriented programming techniques using the Java libraries. The focus of this programming subject is on the creation of robust and effectively constructed Graphical User Interface (GUI) applications that interact with problem domain objects and relational databases. This subject will cover Java GUI components, GUI construction, the interpretation of Unified Modelling Language (UML) class diagrams, streams and serialisation, multithreaded applications, reusable software via JavaBeans, relational database management via the Java Database Connectivity (JDBC) and Java socket programming. In addition, usage of correct object oriented programming heuristics is emphasised in this subject.
learning_outcomes: Design and construct Java Graphical User Interfaces (GUI) that interact with problem domain objects.
Deconstruct/analyse the object-oriented features of a Java program.
Write programs that would communicate with another program running in the network.
Create, manage and manipulate objects via the Java Collections Framework.
Create, connect to and update a relational database using the Java Database Connectivity (JDBC).
Design and implement multithreaded Java applications.
Use the inheritance features of the Java language to design and implement complex object-oriented programs.

title: Programming in Java 2
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Computing, Mathematics and Engineering
syllabus_overview: This subject teaches students to use advanced Java library components in writing object-oriented programs. The focus of this programming subject is on the creation of robust and correctly constructed Graphical User Interface (GUI) applications that interact with problem domain objects and relational databases. This subject will cover Java GUI components, GUI construction, the interpretation of Unified Modelling Language (UML) class diagrams, streams and serialisation, multithreaded applications, and relational database management via the Java Database Connectivity (JDBC) classes. Usage of correct object oriented programming heuristics is emphasised in this subject.
learning_outcomes: Design and implement multithreaded Java applications.
Create, manage and manipulate objects via the Java Collections Framework.
Demonstrate the use of the inheritance features of the Java language to design and implement complex object-oriented programs.
Design and construct Java Graphical User Interfaces (GUI) that interact with problem domain objects.
Create, connect to and update a relational database using the Java Database Connectivity (JDBC).

title: Programming Principles
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Computing, Mathematics and Engineering
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces students to the programming process. It begins with the development of problem solving skills relevant to the solution of programming problems. This subject is one of the foundation subjects for other studies in information technology because it develops skills, techniques and approaches that underpin many other areas of the discipline of computing.
learning_outcomes: Apply sound program analysis, design, coding, debugging, testing and documentation techniques to simple programming problems.
Compare and contrast aspects of the procedural and object oriented programming approaches.
Identify, isolate and correct errors; and evaluate the corrections in all phases of the programming process.
Write code in an appropriate coding language.
Interpret and implement algorithms and program code.
Analyse the steps involved in a disciplined approach to problem-solving, algorithm development and coding.
Demonstrate and explain elements of good programming style.
Apply and justify the concept of object orientation as an approach to data abstraction.

title: Project and Event Management
school: School of Information and Communication Studies
syllabus_overview: This subject is designed to equip students with the skills and understanding to effectively manage projects and events in the information industry. Students will be introduced to phases involved in the lifecycle of projects and events. Students will also learn about different task scheduling techniques and project management software. The applied approach of this subject will help students to effectively manage projects and events in a variety of information contexts.
