learning_outcomes: Distinguish between classical and contemporary theoretical approaches used by sociologists and anthropologists in studying Islam.
Observe and discuss the social and ethnographic dynamics of religion with objectivity.

Comprehend the historical and chronological developments that have influenced the field of sociological and anthropological approaches to religion, including industrialization, secularization, modernity, and postmodernity, with a specific focus on Islam.
Critically assess the views of prominent sociologists and anthropologists on Islam and religion.
Analyse the strengths and weaknesses of the sociology/anthropology of Islam and Islamic sociology/anthropology through conducted studies.
Improve analytical writing and critical thinking skills through written assignments.
Enhance oral presentation and discussion skills through class presentations and discussions.

title: Sociology of Youth
school: School of Social Work and Arts
syllabus_overview: This subject will critically evaluate the position of young people in Australian society, and analyse the development of youth policy during the post WWII period in terms of how society constructs youth as a social problem and politically regulates young people's lives. It will also study youth as social agents, eg as consumers and citizens.
learning_outcomes: Be aware of the ways youth is socially constructed and culturally reproduced.
Have examined the politics and strategies of youth protest and other social movements to initiate social change.
Be aware of demographic changes in Australia and the way they affect young people's life chances.
Have examined how the state and other social institutions politically regulate youth.

title: Software Defined Networking (SDN)
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Computing, Mathematics and Engineering
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces the foundational concepts, architectures, and applications of Software Defined Networking (SDN) in contemporary networked environments. In this subject, students will explore how SDN enables the centralised management and control of network behaviour through software-based architectures and programmable networking approaches. The subject will examines the basic concepts of SDN, including the separation of the control plane from the data plane, controller-based architectures, and the role of physical and virtual network devices in traffic forwarding and network operations. Students will explore the application of SDN in areas such as network automation, cloud computing, virtualisation, resource management, and network security. Students will also develop an understanding of how SDN supports flexible and scalable network management in modern enterprise and distributed network environments.
learning_outcomes: Explain the foundational principles and architectures of Software Defined Networking (SDN)
Describe the separation of control and data planes in software-defined network environments
Analyse how SDN supports network automation and scalability
Identify the role of controllers, APIs, and programmable interfaces in SDN environments
Discuss the application of SDN in contemporary enterprise and distributed network environments.

title: Soil and Rock Mechanics
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: Charles Sturt University Engineering
syllabus_overview: This subject focuses on the behaviour of soils and rocks in civil engineering. Students will learn various tests to determine the engineering properties of soil and rock. Emphasis is on developing students' understanding of the fundamentals of soil and rock behaviour and the skills to analyse civil engineering problems.
learning_outcomes: Classify soils and rocks based on standardized classification systems and test their physical and mechanical properties.
Assess soil settlement and consolidation processes.
Understand the importance of water and the influence of seepage on soil.

title: Software Development Project 1
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Computing, Mathematics and Engineering
syllabus_overview: This subject marks the initial phase of a comprehensive software development endeavour. Students will embark on a journey to create software solutions tailored to the needs of a client sponsor. Working collaboratively in groups, students explore the intricacies of software development methodologies, selecting the most suitable approach for their specific project. With a focus on practical application, students engage in hands-on development, enhancing their programming skills and project management capabilities. This subject lays the foundation for a transition into Software Development Project 2 (ITC309) where the project will be finalised. By the end of ITC303, students are expected to complete the architectural design of their software and present a rudimentary UI/UX demonstration, showcasing the progress and potential of their evolving project.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate software unit and application quality through testing.
Verify design through delivery of a functional prototype.

Identify and apply appropriately the different steps in the project development to produce software, as well as develop the main artifacts of the process, using project management tools to assist in timely completion of milestones.
Analyse and document application requirements using Unified Modelling Language (UML) modelling techniques and tools.
Work effectively in a team environment.
Evaluate and determine suitable technologies to be used in the project.
Support specialist and non-specialist ICT users and stakeholders throughout the project management life cycle through effective communication and documentation.
Apply entrepreneurship skills and attitudes during the planning phase of a project.

title: Software Development Project 2
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Computing, Mathematics and Engineering
syllabus_overview: This subject is the final step in your software engineering project. Work started in ITC303 Software Development Project 1 will be completed in ITC309. This subject, and its linked subject ITC303, cover the practical application of a project management methodology in the development and delivery of a significant project. In particular, the focus of these subjects will be the application of the Unified Process (UP) whereby iterative and incremental development and testing are essential elements of the project lifecycle and process framework. The software development project that students implement should align with their major area (e.g., those majoring in cyber security are expected to implement a software system that relates strongly to cyber security while web development students will need to produce a web-based application). In this subject, students will be working in teams to produce a beta and release of their project, including user and programmer's manuals. They will then be expected to review the project outcomes, artefacts and collaborative work.
learning_outcomes: Use project management tools to assist in timely completion of milestones.
Apply the UP methodology to implement and deploy the software system.
Evaluate the developing project through testing and respond to any defects identified.
Work effectively in a team environment.
Demonstrate technical writing skills in a software development environment through development of user and programmer's manuals.
Evaluate the project process and outcomes, including team management, against the project proposal.

title: Soil Management
school: School of Agricultural, Environmental and Veterinary Sciences
syllabus_overview: In this subject, students will examine the major forms of soil degradation (erosion, acidity, salinity, nutrient decline and deterioration of soil structure) impacting agricultural landscapes. Students will learn and apply the principles of soil fertility and nutrient management within agricultural contexts. Students will further develop skills in interpretation and critical evaluation of soil research data.
learning_outcomes: Develop and justify management options to conserve or improve the soil resource.
Explain the major causes of soil degradation and their management.
Formulate and test hypotheses relating to soil management issues.
Evaluate the quality, and implications, of scientific information relating to soil management issues.

title: Soil Management
school: School of Agricultural, Environmental and Veterinary Sciences
syllabus_overview: In this subject, students will examine the major forms of soil degradation (erosion, acidity, salinity, nutrient decline, deterioration of soil structure and pollution) impacting agricultural landscapes. Students will learn and apply the principles of soil fertility and nutrient management within agricultural contexts. Students will further develop skills in interpretation and critical evaluation of soil research data.
learning_outcomes: Formulate and test complex hypotheses relating to soil management issues.
Develop and justify management options to conserve or improve the soil resource.
Examine and assess the major causes of soil degradation and their management.
Evaluate the quality, and implications, of scientific information relating to soil management issues.

title: Soil Science
school: School of Agricultural, Environmental and Veterinary Sciences
syllabus_overview: This subject provides an introduction to soil science as related to land productivity, sustainability and/or environmental management. Students will be introduced to the physico-chemical properties of soils and their influence on soil fertility and plant growth. Understanding principles of soil formation, distribution and classification are important in determining where different soils are found within a landscape. Students will develop and apply a set of practical skills to determine and report soil qualities for the purpose of soil management/improvement or environmental monitoring.
learning_outcomes: Create and interpret soil maps, including basic soil classification.
Create and interpret soil profile descriptions for the purpose of identifying soil-based restrictions to plant growth.
Describe soil formation processes and their effect on the distribution of soils on the landscape.
Identify and explain the factors contributing to nutrient supply from soils, the cause and effects of waterlogging, soil pH extremes and salinity/sodicity.
Explain how management can influence soil health and plant production.

title: Spatial Design
school: School of Social Work and Arts
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces students to a range of roles and responsibilities in environmental design, including the requisite time and financial planning skills, and computer aided design (CAD) skills and drawing for a range of spatial design outcomes. Students explore the relationship between contextual analysis to the organisational principles of space and place. Students undertake projects through the use of designer-led approaches to the analysis, visualisation and construction of environments, students undertake projects responding to site-specific contextual needs.
learning_outcomes: Produce designs including technical drawing/illustration, utilising CAD and modelling, and other methods.
Describe a range of roles and responsibilities in spatial design.
Execute projects to specific Australian Standards.
Recognise and respond to architectural and other contextual influences.
Creatively respond to design briefs.
Perform contextual needs analysis as an environmental design process.
Explain the relationship between contextual analysis and the organisational principles of space.

title: Solving Problems with Critical Thinking
school: School of Social Work and Arts
syllabus_overview: Critical thinking is a vital skill in all workplaces. This subject introduces students to the fundamentals of critical thinking, including how to think logically, evaluate the reasoning of others, avoid common errors in thought, weigh up options and make decisions well. It also shows how these skills can be used to solve problems, especially those common to professional environments.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate their understanding of the fundamentals of critical thinking through the successful completion of criterion-referenced assessment.
Apply critical thinking skills to solve a problem.

title: Spatial Modelling
school: School of Agricultural, Environmental and Veterinary Sciences
syllabus_overview: In this subject students are introduced to the fundamentals of spatial modelling in the context of environmental and ecological applications. Students learn how to evaluate different approaches to model the distribution of spatial and spatiotemporal data, at different scales. The practical component provides an in-depth understanding of species distribution modelling using machine learning algorithms. It also includes basic spatiotemporal data visualization and analysis. Students completing this subject will have the ability to apply intermediate knowledge and skills in spatial modelling to address projects dealing with environmental and ecological data analysis and mapping.
learning_outcomes: Examine spatial scales and evaluate the impacts in spatial modelling.
Describe, select and critically evaluate species distribution modelling methods.
Describe and evaluate different spatial modelling approaches for environmental and ecological applications, including machine learning.
Describe and evaluate the use of spatiotemporal modelling for environmental and ecological applications.

title: Spatial Project
school: School of Agricultural, Environmental and Veterinary Sciences
syllabus_overview: In this subject, students will develop and execute an independent project, building on previous studies in spatial science. The subject will provide conceptual and practical experience in spatial project management. Each student will identify and undertake an applied spatial project relevant to their own interests. On completion of this subject students will have designed, implemented and critically evaluated their own advanced spatial project.
learning_outcomes: Design, implement and critically evaluate an advanced spatial project.

title: Special Topic 6
school: School of Agricultural, Environmental and Veterinary Sciences
syllabus_overview: This subject provides in-depth study at an advanced level of topics related to the discipline area selected by a student for a Graduate Certificate, Graduate Diploma or Master coursework program.
learning_outcomes: Have a sound knowledge of technical and theory aspects of the nominated topic area.
Evaluate the technical and theoretical knowledge and identify its potential for application to research or practical use.

title: Speech Pathology Practice 2
school: School of Allied Health, Exercise and Sport Sciences
syllabus_overview: In this subject students integrate their speech pathology knowledge and skills, and apply these within speech pathology practice contexts. They complete 24-days of work-integrated learning placement, primarily working with either an adult or paediatric population. Work-integrated learning settings are diverse (e.g., hospitals, community health centres, disability organisations, private practices, education providers, etc.). Students work with practice educators to develop speech pathology knowledge, skills and attributes to a standard of nearing readiness to enter the profession in accordance with current professional standards. In addition, students complete a 5-day specialist clinic that focusses on application of knowledge and skills to a specialist practice area. Throughout the subject, students continue to develop their ability to apply professional conduct, reflective practice, and life-long learning to speech pathology practice.
learning_outcomes: Exhibit the ability to critically analyse, reflect upon, and synthesise developing competency and create and communicate goals and strategies for ongoing learning, to support approaching readiness to enter the profession in accordance with current professional standards.

Demonstrate approaching readiness to enter the profession in accordance with current professional standards, through the ability to transfer speech pathology knowledge, skills and attributes from theory into practice, across practice areas, and across clinical contexts.

Demonstrate approaching readiness to enter the profession in accordance with current professional standards, through application of speech pathology knowledge, skills and attributes to deliver ethical and culturally responsive management of communication and swallowing difficulties for clients across the lifespan.

Integrate the knowledge, skills and attributes for speech pathology professional conduct in accordance with the current professional standards to demonstrate approaching readiness to enter the profession.
prerequisites: SPH531: Intervention for Language and Cognitive Impairments in Speech Pathology
SPH505: Preparation for Speech Pathology Practice
SPH530: Intervention for Sensory-Motor Impairments in Speech Pathology

title: Special Topics 1
school: School of Agricultural, Environmental and Veterinary Sciences
syllabus_overview: This subject provides in-depth study at an advanced level of topics related to the discipline area selected by a student for a Graduate Certificate, Graduate Diploma or Master coursework program. As such for some courses it is used as a capstone subject (i.e. a subject that integrates your prior learning in other subjects). The subject contains no intensive and students should arrange a project supervisor before enrolling in this subject. Students completing this subject will: i) have demonstrated an ability to apply their knowledge and skills with creativity and initiative to new situations in professional practice and/or for further learning and ii) shown an ability to plan and execute a substantial research-based project, capstone experience, and/or piece of scholarship.
learning_outcomes: Have communication and technical research skills to justify and interpret theoretical propositions, methodologies, conclusions and professional decisions to specialist and non-specialist audiences.
Have the ability to apply research principles and methods applicable to a field of work and or learning.
Have demonstrated the application of knowledge and skills with creativity and initiative to new situations in professional practice and/or for further learning.
Have demonstrated the application of knowledge and skills to plan and execute a substantial research-based project, capstone experience and/or piece of scholarship.
Have demonstrated they have a body of knowledge that includes the understanding of recent development in a discipline and/or area of professional practice.

title: Speech Pathology Practice 1
school: School of Allied Health, Exercise and Sport Sciences
syllabus_overview: In this subject, students integrate their speech pathology knowledge and skills, and apply these within speech pathology practice at the Charles Sturt University Speech Pathology Clinic. They complete work-integrated learning with clients from across the lifespan. Under the guidance of practice educators, students work towards developing speech pathology knowledge, skills and attributes to a standard of readiness to enter the profession, in accordance with current professional standards. In addition, students engage with the theory underpinning clinical practice education and reflective practice, providing a strong foundation for ongoing clinical development. This subject emphasises the integration of prior learning and supports students in applying their knowledge and skills to specific populations and areas of speech pathology practice.
learning_outcomes: Integrate and interpret assessment and/or intervention data to establish plans for further assessment or intervention.
Administer formal and informal assessments of communication and swallowing in familiar contexts, in accordance with provided guidelines.
Implement a range of effective therapeutic skills in familiar contexts, with a moderate degree of supervision.

Integrate knowledge, skills and professional attributes, with the support of a practice educator, to plan and deliver speech pathology assessment and intervention appropriate to a specific workplace or population.
Critically reflect on the development of professional competence and identify specific goals and strategies for ongoing learning.
prerequisites: SPH512: Assessment and Analysis of Sensory-Motor Skills in Speech Pathology
SPH513: Assessment and Analysis of Language and Cognition in Speech Pathology

title: Special Topics 7
school: School of Agricultural, Environmental and Veterinary Sciences
syllabus_overview: This subject provides in-depth study at an advanced level of topics related to the discipline area selected by a student for a Graduate Certificate, Graduate Diploma or Master coursework program.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the technical and theoretical knowledge and identify its potential for application to research or practical use.
Have a sound knowledge of technical and theory aspects of the nominated topic area.

title: Speech, Language, and Culture
school: School of Allied Health, Exercise and Sport Sciences
syllabus_overview: This subject encourages students to explore their understanding of speech, language, and culture through self reflection, analysis and discussion of theory plus numerous practical tasks. Students will then apply this understanding to the analysis of samples of spoken interaction involving people with, and without, communication difficulties.
learning_outcomes: Use the International Phonetic Alphabet to transcribe Standard Australian English speech.
Apply knowledge of linguistics, including phonetics, phonology, morphology, syntax, and semantics, to analyse speech and language.
Describe the linguistic context of Australia, and discuss and provide examples of processes of language and cultural contact within Australia.
Identify and describe social, cultural and geographic language varieties and the role of language standardisation and subordination on language attitudes.
Identify and compare institutional and academic perspectives on speech, language and culture.

title: Speech Pathology Practice 3
school: School of Allied Health, Exercise and Sport Sciences
syllabus_overview: In this subject, students will consolidate their speech pathology knowledge and skills, and apply these within speech pathology practice contexts. They complete 24-days of work-integrated learning placement, in a different practice setting to SPH515 (Speech Pathology Practice 2), primarily working with either an adult or paediatric population. Work-integrated learning settings are diverse (e.g., hospitals, community health centres, disability organisations, private practices, education providers, etc.). Students work with practice educators to develop speech pathology knowledge, skills and attributes to a standard of readiness to enter the profession in accordance with current professional standards. In addition, students complete a 5-day specialist clinic that focusses on application of knowledge and skills to a specialist practice area that is different to the one completed in SPH515 (Speech Pathology Practice 2). Throughout these experiences, students consolidate their ability to transfer professional conduct, reflective practice, and life-long learning skills to speech pathology practice with novel clients, and in novel contexts, to demonstrate their readiness to enter the profession with reference to current professional standards.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate the speech pathology knowledge, skills and attributes for readiness to enter the profession, with regards to professional conduct, in accordance with the current professional standards.

Demonstrate the speech pathology knowledge, skills and attributes for readiness to enter the profession, in the delivery of ethical and culturally responsive management of communication and swallowing difficulties for clients across the lifespan, in accordance with the current professional standards.

Consistently exhibit the ability to critically analyse, reflect upon, and synthesise developing competency and create and communicate goals and strategies for ongoing learning, to support approaching readiness to enter the profession in accordance with current professional standards.

Demonstrate readiness to enter the profession in accordance with current professional standards, through the ability to transfer speech pathology knowledge, skills and attributes from theory into practice, across practice areas, and across clinical contexts.
prerequisites: SPH517: Introduction to workplace learning in speech pathology (year-long subject)
SPH515: Integrating Speech Pathology Competency in the Workplace

title: Spiritual Direction in the Christian Tradition
school: School of Theology
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces the nature and practice of spiritual direction. It examines the tradition of spiritual direction as a way of listening, discernment, and responding to God and others. It provides historical background, and an overview of different approaches to spirituality in the Christian tradition. It considers techniques of prayer and meditation and the process of spiritual direction. Personal qualities of a good director are discussed and practised, and the spiritual dimension in pastoral ministry is explored.
learning_outcomes: Outline and evaluate their own understanding of the ministry of spiritual direction in various contexts, eg. suffering.
Outline and discuss critically the ministry of spiritual direction and the place it holds within contemporary Christian churches.
Demonstrate research, writing and communication skills.
Reflect critically on their own experience of the spiritual life.
Discuss various techniques of prayer and meditation in the Christian tradition.
Examine and discuss critically a variety of historical models of spiritual direction from the Christian tradition.
Outline and evaluate the spiritual dimension in pastoral ministry.

title: Sports Media 1
school: School of Allied Health, Exercise and Sport Sciences
syllabus_overview: Sports Media 1 introduces students to the historical and contemporary connections between sport and the media and serves as a foundation for further study in this field. Sport and media have a unique connection, as sport and all forms of media have changed each other and continue to do so. It is impossible to describe sport and media as discreet independent social institutions, rather, as overlapping and corporate organisations. This subject explores prominent sports journalists in history and their reporting style, the impact of television on sports, the contemporary nature of sports journalism, investigative sports journalism and the notion of sports media as the 'toy department' of news. Sports Media 1 provides students with knowledge of the complex interrelationship between sport and media, particularly in relation to concepts of gender and culture.
learning_outcomes: Describe the ways in which sport influences media landscapes.
Describe the changing landscape of sports media as a professional practice.
Compare and contrast the significant and pivotal historical developments in the relationship between sport and the media.
Articulate informed opinions about the positive and negative consequences of the mediatisation of professional sport, and how ethical conduct relates to this mediatisation.
Investigate and explain the ways that recent developments in technology, such as digital cultures, are reshaping sports media.

title: Sports Media 2
school: School of Allied Health, Exercise and Sport Sciences
syllabus_overview: Sports Media 2 gives students an opportunity to develop and apply skills in two areas of sports journalism media. Students will analyse critiques of the industry and the use of text, sound and images in modern sports journalism and sports media. The subject also requires students to produce their own examples of sports media product. Students will critique the contemporary culture of sports media in Australia and globally, consider how cultural power works in the relationship between sport and media, contemplate how notions of gender, sexuality and discrimination affect sports media and also examine new spaces in which sports media operate (particularly online spaces). Sports Media 2 provides students with the opportunity to critically reflect on the changing landscapes on sports media and also prepares students for ethical and professional workplace experiences.
learning_outcomes: Critically reflect on the economic relationship of sport and media, and how cultural power and globalisation affects such relationships.
Analyse the use of text, sound and images in sports media.
Utilise research to develop their own ideas about the newsworthiness of sports stories and develop their own 'angles'.
Respond to and implement feedback on their own sports journalism product and professional practice.
Critically analyse the construction of narrative and 'good writing' in sports media contexts.
Plan, develop and produce their own sports journalism product in clear, concise and unambiguous professional communication according to the rules of the relevant genre of sports media.

title: Spotlight on Design and Content Creation
school: School of Information and Communication Studies
syllabus_overview: The subject introduces students to the discipline of design and content creation by addressing three important questions: what is content creation? how can we build connections with others through content? and, how is content designed, produced and distributed? This subject introduces the key concepts of content design, production and publication for a range of media channels.
learning_outcomes: Generate ideas and gather information to write and produce content for a variety of media.
Follow a basic process for developing content.
Articulate the history, context and purpose of design and content creation.
Demonstrate the fundamental skills of a content creator.

title: Spotlight on Journalism
school: School of Information and Communication Studies
syllabus_overview: The subject introduces students to the discipline of journalism by addressing three important questions: what is journalism; what is its role in society; and how is it produced and distributed? This subject introduces the key concepts of news, production and publication in a range of media channels.
learning_outcomes: Communicate with clarity and purpose using appropriate research, evidence, language, grammar and formats in developing news content.
Investigate and source information and ideas to inform the development of news content.
Demonstrate the ability to develop stories and multi-media content to satisfy news values and objectives.
Explain the contemporary media landscape and the issues impacting the design and production of news content.
Apply the legal and ethical guidelines in formulating news content.

title: Spotlight on Strategic Communication
school: School of Information and Communication Studies
syllabus_overview: The subject introduces students to the discipline of strategic communication by addressing three important questions: what is strategic communication?; what is its role in society?; and, how is communication planned, produced and executed? This subject explores the processes that inform professional communication for purpose and impact.
learning_outcomes: Generate ideas and information to execute the communication planning cycle.
Articulate the history, context and purpose of strategic communication.
Demonstrate the fundamental skills of a strategic communicator.
Follow a basic process for developing strategic communication.

title: Statistical Data Analysis
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Computing, Mathematics and Engineering
syllabus_overview: This subject explores the use of statistical techniques to answer questions posed by researchers. It starts by determining the types of data to be collected and how this should be done to maximise the information obtained. It then considers various methods of statistical data analysis that might be required and considers their underlying assumptions, the situations in which they may be appropriate and what results can be obtained. Emphasis will be placed on interpreting these results, communicating with colleagues and using a statistical package. The methods of design and analysis will be illustrated by case studies. The learning will be motivated by applying the subject material to a practical experiment.
learning_outcomes: Use a commonly available statistical computer package to perform the analyses.
Explain the fundamental differences between observational studies and experimental designs, including the advantages and disadvantages of each.
Design a data collection process in consultation with colleagues so as to maximise the information obtained for a specified cost.
Interpret the results of a statistical analysis and be able to explain the conclusions to someone without statistical training.
Describe the role of statistical methodology in scientific investigations.
Identify and apply appropriate methods of statistical analysis to data that arise in a variety of research situations.

title: Statistical Techniques
school: School of Information and Communication Studies
syllabus_overview: Extends and deepens students knowledge of experimental design, analysis of variance and regression. Multiple regression and the connection between analysis of variance and regression is covered. Multiple comparisons, contrasts, orthogonal contrasts, multiple degree of freedom components, model diagnostic checking and variance stabilizing transformations are included. The analysis of variance methods cover: one-way ANOVA, two-way ANOVA, randomised complete blocks, factorial designs, Latin squares, Graeco-Latin squares, Balanced incomplete blocks, Youden squares, and Nesterd ANOVA. An alternative method for comparing different ANOVA designs, using multiple regression, and computer applications using MINITAB, are also included.
learning_outcomes: Understand aspects of those designed experiments most commonly used in scientific and industrial work.
Explain linear modelling through the use of regression methods similar to those in standard computing packages.
Have an appreciation of the models behind analysis of variance.

title: Standing Operating Procedures: Training and Exercise Development
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: Australian Graduate School of Policing Security
syllabus_overview: This subject provides the skills and knowledge to develop standard operating procedures (SOP), identify and develop training needs and develop an exercise to test plans and procedures. This will include the development of SOP for the management of emergency situations; defining the relationship of SOP to community/ enterprise emergency management plans; identifying the training requirements of organisations and personnel who have roles within plans and SOP; and developing exercises to test the specific emergency management plans and SOP.
learning_outcomes: Generate standard operating procedures for the management of emergency situations.
Analyse the training requirements and practices in an organisation.
Develop training exercises to test Emergency Management plans.

title: Statutory Classes Underwriting Management
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Business
syllabus_overview: This subject provides the student with the knowledge and skills to assess and underwrite risk relating to Statutory Classes and to survey risk exposure and interpret portfolio performance.
learning_outcomes: Calculate rates and premiums.
Review operational performance of policies and portfolios.
Evaluate the impact of the legislation on insurers.
Respond to and participate in reviews / appeals on rating decisions.
Identify and discuss the principles of workers compensation and Compulsory Third Party insurance.
Evaluate the risk exposures inherent in Statutory Classes.

title: Statutory Classes Claims Management
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Business
syllabus_overview: This subject provides the student with the knowledge and skills to manage and resolve claims in Statutory Classes
learning_outcomes: Process treaty claims.
Define terms and concepts of Statutory Classes' claims.
Participate in negotiations to settle claims.
Review claims settlement policy and procedures.
Apply legal terms and concepts to Statutory Classes claims management.
Ro process claims and finalise settlement.
Evaluate nonroutine claims.
Resolve claims disputes.

title: Step into Uni
school: School of Education
syllabus_overview: ‘Step into Uni’ is one of four modular subjects in the Access Charles Sturt Entry course. It explicitly teaches students how to access and navigate university systems and learning technologies to successfully undertake and complete coursework and administration tasks. Each module progressively supports the development of core skills including independent online learning, time management, effective communication, help seeking strategies and awareness of the principles of academic integrity. Students will develop confidence with online learning tools, familiarity with the learning and life resources provided by the university, understanding of the expectations of assessment, and insight into their own learning needs and capacities.
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose and expectations of university learning and teaching.
Apply a range of learning and help seeking strategies to support successful participation in learning and university life.
Communicate appropriately in an academic or professional setting for designated purposes.
Access and navigate university systems, digital tools and media to complete learning and admin tasks.

title: Stepping into Statistics
school: School
syllabus_overview: This subject will review the necessary mathematics and statistics prerequisite skills required by students about to study subjects including Business Statistics (QBM117), Scientific Statistics (STA201), Mathematics and Statistics in Health Sciences (MTH135). The topics to be covered include calculator skills, basic algebra, introductory statistics, sigma notation, inequalities, straight line graphs and introductory probability.
learning_outcomes: Utilise services available at Charles Sturt University.
Understand and work with algebraic expressions.
Use a calculator confidently and correctly.
Understand concepts of basic probability.

title: Strategic Accounting for Enterprise Management
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Business
syllabus_overview: This subject emphasises the role of accounting in management decision making, particularly in providing information and analysis to support strategic management activity and the role of social and environmental accounting to support sustainability strategies. These highlight the changing role of accountants and the challenge in balancing the needs of management, customers, employees, shareholders and other stakeholders with ethical and legal concerns. The use of accounting information to evaluate existing competitive strategies, develop new strategies, and monitor and assess progress towards chosen organisational solutions will be explored. This subject requires the student to synthesise and integrate the theory and practice learned in subjects undertaken in the Accounting degree to understand, structure and resolve problems for organisations operating with a sustainable business model.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the impact of the international business environment, global competitiveness and societal and cultural expectations on management accounting in regional, national and multinational organisations.
Use strategic management principles and technologies in making and assessing business decisions for profit and not for profit organisations.
Generate, evaluate and use information for planning and controlling operations within an organisation.
Generate, evaluate and use quantitative and qualitative information to measure financial and non financial performance of an organisation.
Apply sustainability concepts in the context of accounting and business practices.
Develop and evaluate computer spreadsheet models which aid business decision analysis and communicate clearly and concisely the outcomes to a range of stakeholders.

title: Strategic and Contemporary Financial Issues
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Business
syllabus_overview: This subject aims to encapsulate learning from students' previous studies. Topics covered are chosen from current finance issues which are of strategic importance to the finance industry and industry professionals. The subject requires students to critically review the print and electronic media concerning contemporary finance topics and analyse the implications of these issues. Case studies and other learning methods will be used throughout. The subject builds on the knowledge acquired in FIN516 Corporate Finance and FIN530 Financial Markets and Instruments.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse and provide informed commentary on empirical evidence from financial media, industry sources and empirical studies.
Explain and synthesise the emerging issues and complexities that arise in the Australian and global corporate finance sectors.
Analyse and explain the nature of current finance issues and make strategic choices based on the evidence.

title: Strategic and Sustainable Accounting
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Business
syllabus_overview: This subject emphasises the role of accounting in management decision making, particularly in providing information and analysis to support strategic management activity and the role of social and environmental accounting to support sustainability strategies. These highlight the changing role of accountants and the challenge in balancing the needs of management, customers, employees, shareholders and other stakeholders with ethical and legal concerns. The use of accounting information to evaluate existing competitive strategies, develop new strategies, and monitor and assess progress towards chosen organisational solutions. This subject requires the student to synthesise and integrate the theory and practice learned in subjects undertaken in the Accounting degree to understand, structure and resolve problems for organisations operating with a sustainable business model.
learning_outcomes: Generate, evaluate and use quantitative and qualitative information to measure financial and non financial performance of an organisation.
Use strategic management principles and technologies in making and assessing business decisions for profit and not for profit organisations.
Develop and evaluate computer spreadsheet models which aid business decision analysis.
Apply sustainability concepts in the context of accounting and business practices.
Generate, evaluate and use information for planning and controlling operations within an organisation.

Analyse the impact of the international business environment, global competitiveness and societal and cultural expectations on management accounting in regional, national and multinational organisations.

title: Strategic Business Development
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Business
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces key practical and theoretical aspects of strategic business decision making. Students will understand how an organisation's mission, strategies and objectives provide an overarching framework for the development of the planning process. Students will undertake an in-depth situational analysis; considering theoretical business models such as sustainable competitive advantage and current industry trends. This approach allows for the development of innovative and entrepreneurial ways of thinking as well as knowledge and skills in the areas of strategic analysis, strategic choice and strategic implementation.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate and apply theories of strategic planning.
Assess the impact of contemporary industry issues including sustainability, diversity in markets and ethics on decision-makers.
Identify and differentiate between functional business units and evaluate how they should act conjointly to achieve organisation's strategic aims and objectives.
Develop and clearly communicate a strategic plan for a business.
prerequisites: BUS204: Business Analysis and Data Analytics

title: Strategic Business Research
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Business
syllabus_overview: Business research plays an important role in informing strategic business decisions for managers, marketers, human resource advisors, analysts and other business professionals. Research can be used more effectively if managers understand the processes and techniques that have generated research findings. This subject introduces the principles of business research methods. Students will develop the skills needed to identify the research problem, plan, design, and implement a business research project and analyse and interpret the findings. Quantitative, qualitative and contemporary research methods are examined. The principles of ethics in research and research report writing are also addressed.
learning_outcomes: Work independently and/or collaboratively to plan, design and report on a research project.
Work independently and/or collaboratively to collect and synthesise insights from a range of sources relating to a business problem.
Work independently and/or collaboratively to assess ethical issues in business research.
Work independently and/or collaboratively to Identify research opportunities contextualised within the business and aligned to strategic goals.
Work independently and/or collaboratively to select and justify processes and techniques associated with contemporary business research methodologies.
prerequisites: MKT560: Big Data and Marketing analytics

title: Strategic Communication Perspectives 1
school: School of Information and Communication Studies
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces students' knowledge, skills and abilities to design and create a strategic communication solution to achieve specific objectives. Students learn how to conceptualise, plan, design, resource and evaluate a communication strategy to reach a particular audience. Students learn the importance of relationship and issues management in implementing a communication strategy.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate evidence of implementing, reflecting and evaluating communication strategy.
Demonstrate approaches to managing professional relationships and issues.
Demonstrate the interpersonal and communication skills of a strategic communicator.
Undertake research and discern information to develop evidence-based strategy.
Conceptualise, plan, resource and implement a communication strategy.

title: Strategic Event Management
school: School of Information and Communication Studies
syllabus_overview: This subject develops students' ability to plan and stage an event, emphasising the strategic value of events and the importance of planning at every stage. This subject provides students with sound knowledge of event management processes and a broad range of event-related skills. This subject is designed with adaptable delivery models, which may include combinations of condensed online sessions and one-off workshops.
learning_outcomes: Devise and implement message strategies to communicate to stakeholders through an event.
Apply strategic planning and project management skills in executing a real or simulated event.

title: Strategic Human Resource Management
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Business
syllabus_overview: If Human Resource Strategy and Organisational Strategy are not aligned then organisations will ultimately struggle to deliver their mission. This subject examines the importance of aligning these strategies and practices. A key focus is the need for the HR function to be able to measure and specify its actual contribution to achieving organisational change and success. This is a capstone subject in HRM and it is recommended students complete it at the end of their course.
learning_outcomes: Align HR activities with overall organisational strategy by developing, planning and applying contextualised strategic solutions to specific organisational human resource challenges.
Analyse organisational and human resource strategies, and perform a strategic gap analysis.
Measure and quantify the contribution of HR activity at an organisational level.
Evaluate the differing strategic contributions of particular HR disciplines.

title: Strategic Financial Management
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Business
syllabus_overview: This subject examines the principle of adding value for shareholders through the selective restructuring of assets, liabilities and capital in the corporate organisation. The subject uses a case study method of instruction to expose students to actual financial decision making situations. In this way students draw on knowledge gained in previous subjects to analyse problems and strategic issues faced by the financial manager in the contemporary business environment.
learning_outcomes: Analyse financial data and provide a decision on a course of action that is in the best interest of firm shareholders.
Analyse and account for risk in the decision making process.
Evaluate real world issues and problems faced by the financial manager, by being able to select appropriate financial techniques.
Explain how financial management relates to general corporate policy.

title: Strategic Communication Perspectives 2
school: School of Information and Communication Studies
syllabus_overview: This subject develops students' capabilities in conceptualising communication campaigns through exploring the strategic and tactics aspects of campaigns, the theories underpinning campaign development, delivery and evaluation. Students learn to apply strategic planning models in designing integrated strategic communication campaigns involving a range of multimedia and multimodal communication activities. Students investigate contemporary thinking about strategy, the role of research, stakeholder engagement, issues management, consultation and collaboration in developing communication strategies.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate the developing skills of a strategic communication professional.
Reflect on their practice as a strategic communication professional.
Plan and deliver the production of strategic communication for a variety of media on real world projects.

title: Strategic Human Resource Management
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Business
syllabus_overview: This subject emphasises the role of the human resource management professional in the strategy development and implementation process. A range of concepts, theories and models which aim to integrate the various functional areas of human resource management with business strategy will be examined. A variety of issues and challenges in the development of a strategic approach to human resource management practice are explored.
learning_outcomes: Identify crucial stakeholders at all levels (internally and externally), make informed decisions, influence outcomes, and offer input into business strategy.

Analyse and evaluate an organisation's business strategy to produce informed, relevant and well-communicated business advice relating to the application of ethical and sustainable strategic human resource management.
Evaluate human resource management strategies to determine impact and outcomes on overall business short and long term strategies.
Explain the meaning of strategic human resource management and the role human resource managers should play in carrying out the strategic objectives of the organisation.

title: Strategic Management
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Business
syllabus_overview: The subject introduces the strategic planning function within an organisation. This includes consideration of an organisation's internal resources as well as the external factors which impact upon strategic decision making. The formulation, implementation and selection of strategic alternatives which mesh with these factors is also examined. This subject may include some face to face workshops and activities depending on the student cohort.
learning_outcomes: Identify and examine underlying assumptions that underpin strategic management.
Apply and critically analyse strategic management concepts and models.
Reflect on learning, and integrate prior knowledge and skills, to develop strategic recommendations.

title: Strategic Marketing and Planning
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Business
syllabus_overview: This subject focuses on strategic approaches to marketing management and deals with the process of developing and implementing a marketing strategy. Further, it examines how these processes can be managed to gain and sustain superior performance in the competitive market place. A closer examination of the business mission, strategies and objectives provide a framework for the development of the strategic marketing planning process. An in depth situation analysis combined with concepts such as market segmentation and sustainable competitive advantage provide input into the marketing strategy decision process.
learning_outcomes: Devise marketing strategies to achieve organisational objectives using a range of strategic assessment tools and informational resources.
Identify and explain the relationship between strategic marketing planning and organisational strategy.
Explain the concept of market orientation and its relevance to various functions/departments within an organisation.
Apply appropriate tools to analyse and better understand both the external and internal environments of a business.
Contextualise strategic marketing across a range of organisational types and settings to develop competitive advantage.

title: Strategic Marketing Management
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Business
syllabus_overview: This capstone subject focuses on strategic approaches to marketing management. The business mission, strategies and objectives provide an overarching framework for the development of the strategic marketing planning process. An in-depth situation analysis combined with concepts such as the value chain and sustainable competitive advantage provide input into the marketing strategy decision process. A review of the marketing plan, together with its implementation and control is undertaken.
learning_outcomes: Contextualise strategic marketing across a range of organisational types to develop competitive advantage.
Identify and explain the relationship between strategic marketing planning and organisational strategy to deliver on stated objectives.
Critically review contemporary decision making methods and models, and to demonstrate how relationships, alliances and organisation capability enhance strategic marketing opportunity.
Develop an integrated strategic marketing plan with appropriate and measurable strategic marketing goals.
Devise marketing strategies to achieve organisational objectives using a range of strategic assessment tools and informational resources and through appreciation of dynamic external environments.

title: Strategic People Management
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Business
syllabus_overview: The subject introduces the strategic nature of managing people who report directly to front line managers. It covers work allocation, methods to review performance, rewarding excellence and providing constructive feedback where improvement is identified. The subject makes the link between performance management and development to ensure key result areas and key performance indicators and standards are set and adhered to in a way that supports a positive organisational culture.
learning_outcomes: Reflect on learning, and integrate prior knowledge and skills to attract, retain and motivate staff, and make appropriate recommendations in consultation with relevant stakeholders.
Apply and critically analyse performance management systems.
Identify and outline relevant legislative and regulatory requirements, including modern awards and enterprise agreements, related to managing people.

title: Strategic Practice
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Business
syllabus_overview: This subject introduces some of the key practical and theoretical aspects of strategic management for those working in the IT field. It provides an overview of key forces and debates that have produced, and continue to influence the development of, strategic management. Potential benefits and limitations of strategic management will be addressed. This approach allows for the development of knowledge and skills in the areas of strategic analysis, strategic choice and strategic implementation.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate a capacity to play a number of roles in relation to strategic management.
Describe and organise the various components of strategic management and their inter-relationships.
Produce strategic alternatives, evaluate them, and make recommendations from them.
Undertake internal and external strategic analysis.

Identify and evaluate how functional areas such as marketing, finance, operations and human resource management should act conjointly toward the attainment of an organisation's strategic aims and objectives.
Critically evaluate the parts and the whole, the importance of developing strategically appropriate relationships between people, processes, functions, structures and even organisations.
Describe and critique the process of strategic management for the realisation of organisational change and/or success in the private, public, and not-for-profit sectors.

Outline and explain the evolution of ideas and practices leading to the development of strategic management of information technology and its relationship to other management practices and principles.

title: Strategic Thinking in Design
school: School of Social Work and Arts
syllabus_overview: In this subject students will explore and engage in technical graphic design and production processes in practical design-led projects. Working to briefs, students will analyse design contexts and situational needs in reference to professional, economic, societal and environmental influences, and ethical considerations. A focus on strategic design choices and decision making will include the selection and creative application of suitable software required to meet industry standards.
learning_outcomes: Select and deploy appropriate communication strategies and technologies for project teams and stakeholders.
Analyse design contexts and situational needs to develop appropriate design solutions.
Apply creative and technical skills required in the production of industry standard computer-based designs.
Justify design decisions in reference to ethical, professional, economic, societal and environmental influences and impacts.
Plan, manage and document technical graphic design projects to a brief.

title: Strategic Thinking, Analysis and Action
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Business
syllabus_overview: This subject builds understanding and appreciation of effective university strategic leadership and management, within both the external and CSU context. Participants will develop knowledge and skills in the areas of strategic analysis, strategic choice and strategic implementation. In this subject particular attention is given to participants' leadership role in sharing knowledge, and leading others to develop and implement strategy and practise sustainability for longer-term organisational outcomes within the context of resource restraints and a highly politicised tertiary environment.
learning_outcomes: Plan, initiate and evaluate their strategic leadership practice, actions and projects to align with and respond to the complex and dynamic internal (CSU) and external environment.
Generate, communicate and implement original strategic solutions using collaborative and contemporary approaches to strategic management within their current leadership situation.
Identify and explain the key components of strategic management such as strategy analysis, strategy formulation and strategy implementation, and their interrelationships.
Critically examine alternative strategies that encourage sustainable practice within resource constraints and organisational capability.

title: Strategy and Corporate Governance
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Business
syllabus_overview: The purpose of this subject is to consolidate and broaden students' understanding of business, particularly in regards to strategic approaches. Students are encouraged to think more broadly about the concept of strategy, and apply their knowledge about industries and companies to the concepts and theories covered in the subject. The subject logically proceeds through concepts of strategic management, analysing the industry and company situation, and then crafting a strategy in a domestic or international environment. The issues of ethics, corporate social responsibility and sustainability are also considered.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate and explain the key components of strategic management such as situational analysis, strategy formulation and strategy implementation, and their interrelationships.
Apply analytical tools to analyse the external environment and internal situation of a business.
Analyse and explain the complexities of ethics, CSR (corporate social responsibility) and environmental sustainability in strategic management.
Compare and contrast how different competitive strategies allow a business to build competitive advantage and deliver superior value to customers.
Differentiate how changes in market conditions across countries can influence strategic choices in international markets.

title: Strategies for Organisational Behaviour
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Business
syllabus_overview: This subject develops students knowledge, understanding and skills relating to human behaviour within organisations at the individual, group and organisational levels. The subject examines the factors which influence behaviour such as leadership, teamwork, motivation, change, power and learning. Strategies which may be adopted to increase personal and organisational effectiveness will also be discussed.
learning_outcomes: Assess the role of work teams and groups in an organisation and recommend strategies to manage performance of teams and groups.
Identify and explain contemporary Organisational Behaviour (OB) theories and concepts about behaviour of people in organisations as individuals or as members of collective groups and cultures.
Assess effective practices of an organisation, identify key issues and formulate and apply appropriate managerial strategies for enhancing the performance of an organisation and its people.
Reflect on your own behaviour and that of others within organisations based on OB theories and concepts.
Explain what motivates individuals' behaviour in organisations and create suggestions for managing their behaviour based on OB theories and concepts.

title: Strategy and Planning
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: School of Business
syllabus_overview: Today's organisations operate in a global, digital economy where the pace of change and disruptive events can significantly impact business success. This subject introduces the key practical and theoretical issues of strategic planning processes in contemporary environments. This subject helps students to gain and apply knowledge to understand how organisations plan, formulate, implement, and manage business strategy in order to fulfil key stakeholders expectations and achieve sustainable business success. The subject addresses planned versus emergent strategy, revolutionary versus evolutionary change, and organisational perpetuation versus transformation. Students develop key leadership skills in analysis, choice, design and implementation of business strategy in complex environments.
learning_outcomes: Analyse organisational forces that may inhibit or support the implementation of organisational strategy and make recommendations for sustainable business success.
Critically review and apply theoretical frameworks to conduct strategic planning in the context of traditional and disruptive environments.
Consult collaboratively to identify limitations of existing strategy and justify recommendations for strategic change.
Analyse the internal and external environments to assess the health of the organisation's strategy and plans.
Identify and critique key aspects of an existing organisation's strategy.

title: Strength of Materials
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: Charles Sturt University Engineering
syllabus_overview: This subject builds upon the foundational knowledge acquired in the introductory subject and examines material behaviour and structural analysis. The subject is designed to further enhance the understanding of mechanical properties and loading conditions encountered in engineering practice.
learning_outcomes: Use buckling, stability analysis, and finite element analysis to understand complex structural behaviour and design considerations.
Utilise energy methods to analyse statically indeterminate structures.
Apply beam theory concepts to analyse and design structural components subjected to bending and shear forces.

title: Strengthening Primary Health Care with Rural Communities
school: School of Nursing, Paramedicine and Healthcare Sciences
syllabus_overview: Students will explore contemporary perspectives of Primary Health Care as a whole of society approach to health. This subject provides students with the opportunity to examine and critique delivery of Primary Health Care services in the context in which they live and practice, with an emphasis on regional, rural and remote communities. Students will explore the importance of working and consulting with communities and other key service providers to support optimal health and outcomes, with a focus on respectful engagement and consultation with First Nations and other marginalised populations.
learning_outcomes: Identify and present contemporary research evaluating the delivery and sustainability of primary health care services in regional, rural and remote communities.
Critique current primary health care practice focused on illness prevention, health promotion and health education for regional, rural and remote communities and populations.
Critically evaluate the importance of global, national and regional policies and perspectives of Primary Health Care reforms for enabling healthy rural communities.
Identify and critique the delivery of Primary Health Care services in the context in which they live and practice.
Engage and consult respectfully with First Nations, migrant/refugee, and marginalised populations to support optimal health.
prerequisites: NRS535: Primary Health Care: A Pathway to Better Health
NRS535: Primary Health Care: A Pathway to Better Health

title: Structures and the Effects of Fire
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: Australian Graduate School of Policing Security
syllabus_overview: The aim of this subject is to equip the student with advanced knowledge of the impact of fire on buildings and building materials, and the behaviour of buildings and building components affected by fire. Through this subject students will develop the knowledge required to professionally investigate fires involving buildings and a variety of building component materials. Fire patterns associated with different types of fires will be explored.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of the theoretical concepts and underpinnings relevant to building behaviour and fire investigation.
Review, critically analyse, consolidate and synthesise knowledge about the effects of fire on building components and safety aspects related to fire affected buildings.
Demonstrate mastery in the recognition and critical analysis of the various phases of the combustion process involved in the spread of fire through buildings and from building to building.

title: Student Learning and Engagement
school: School of Education
syllabus_overview: This subject examines the nature of the school environment and introduces teacher education students to the ways in which teachers plan for effective learning and communicate as professionals in this environment. Students will engage with strategies for teaching and learning, classroom management, planning and assessment. Students will undertake 160 hours of supervised placement in a primary classroom. During this placement, students will apply their developing understandings of curriculum, child development and the Australian Professional Standards for Teachers in their planning and teaching, and utilise a range of effective learning and assessment strategies to engage and cater for diverse learners.
learning_outcomes: Plan and implement learning activities for effective teaching and learning.
Demonstrate beginning skills essential for clear communication, managing student learning, learning environments and professional relationships.
Create a folio of evidence of development towards achieving the Australian Professional Standards for Teachers.
Assess and provide feedback on student learning.
Create and maintain supportive and safe learning environments.
Reflect on their development as a teacher and establish learning goals for their professional experience placement.
Apply a range of effective teaching strategies for diverse learners in the design and implementation of lessons.
Engage in critical enquiry and dialogue with a range of educational professionals such as subject coordinator, university liaison officer and supervising teacher.
Report an overall rating of satisfactory in a professional experience placement of 160 hours in a primary classroom.

title: Studies in Liturgy and Worship
school: School of Theology
syllabus_overview: This subject provides students with the opportunity to engage with contemporary scholarship on the interrelationship of worship and theology, developed through an appreciation of worship as 'primary theology'. Necessarily this involves an in-depth understanding of the range of liturgical sources including prayers, lectionaries, rites, rubrics, music and performance, art and architecture, along with the development of skills in analysing their content, influence and contribution to theology.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an in-depth theological understanding of the interrelationship between liturgy and doctrine.
Develop appropriate tools and methods for the critical analysis of liturgical texts and performance.
Evaluate critically current scholarship in liturgical theology.
Identify and critically evaluate a range of liturgical texts, e.g., prayers, lectionaries, rites, rubrics, music, liturgical space, art and performance.
Demonstrate an appreciation of the place of culture in worship.

title: Studies in Liturgy and Worship
school: School of Theology
syllabus_overview: This subject provides students with the opportunity to engage with contemporary scholarship on the interrelationship of worship and theology, developed through an appreciation of worship as 'primary theology'. Necessarily this involves an in-depth understanding of the range of liturgical sources including prayers, lectionaries, rites, rubrics, music and performance, art and architecture, along with the development of skills in analysing their content, influence and contribution to theology.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an appreciation of the place of culture in worship.
Identify and critically evaluate a range of liturgical texts, e.g., prayers, lectionaries, rites, rubrics, music, liturgical space, art and performance.
Develop appropriate tools and methods for the critical analysis of liturgical texts and performance.
Evaluate critically current scholarship in liturgical theology.
Demonstrate an in-depth theological understanding of the interrelationship between liturgy and doctrine.

title: Studio Lighting Design
school: School of Social Work and Arts
syllabus_overview: This subject covers professional photographic studio skills and practices with emphasis on hands-on technique and technical theory which includes location and studio flash lighting, colour temperature manipulation and sophisticated photographic projects. This subject provides fundamental knowledge of the relationship between the physical properties of light and human visual perception with a focus on the creative use of lighting for photography and design. The subject covers requisite workplace health and safety requirements for site specific lighting work in real world scenarios.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate their understanding of the principles of natural and artificial lighting, and effectively apply these in and out of the studio in a creative context.
Demonstrate an understanding of the use of colour temperature manipulation in photographic imaging.
Demonstrate the use of lighting as a creative medium.
Demonstrate the creative application of sophisticated digital imaging processing and enhancement skills.
Generate and document lighting designs in response to creative briefs.
Describe the relationship between the physical properties of light and human visual perception.

title: Studio Research and Seminar
school: School of Social Work and Arts
syllabus_overview: This subject is designed to enable the student to demonstrate the ability to apply and synthesise technical and conceptual knowledge through research into contemporary and historical arts practices including drawing, design, new media, animation, jewellery and photography. The outcome will be a focused body of new work(s) in their second major area of study when completing a double degree.
learning_outcomes: Be capable of working collaboratively and independently in challenging current arts and design practices through the use of appropriate technologies.
Demonstrate the ability to exercise reflective and critical judgement as it applies to their selected field of study.
Demonstrate an understanding of the position of their selected major field of study nationally and internationally.

title: Successful Teaching
school: School of Education
syllabus_overview: This subject focuses on the principles and practices of the profession of teaching and the Australian Professional Standards for Teachers, and their relationship and alignment with the CSU Graduate Learning Outcomes (GLOs). The subject provides students with the opportunity to critically engage with key ideas about the CSU GLOs in the context of the profession of teaching, responding to key curriculum priorities, and how teaching knowledge and skill develops with professional practice and reflection. Students have opportunities to identify and examine a range of evidence-based teaching and learning strategies employed in teaching school students, and review how, when, where and why selected teaching and learning strategies are implemented in teaching contexts. Students develop and evaluate core teaching and learning strategies in relation to developing key literacy and numeracy skills in a learning activities sequence, and align these to the specificities of the classroom context and their teaching area. This subject provides a platform for students to build upon as they develop and extend their knowledge and skills in the profession of teaching over the remainder of their teacher education course. While this subject engages with all of the Australian Professional Standards for Teachers, it specifically contributes toward the achievement of: 1.1, 2.1, 2.2, 2.5, 2.6, 3.2, 3.3, 3.4, 3.5, 7.3 and 7.4, at the graduate level.
learning_outcomes: Explain the ways core teaching and learning strategies can be adapted for diverse classroom settings in a curriculum area.
Design and develop a sequence of learning activities using knowledge of effective teaching and learning strategies and resources.
Examine and assess a range of teaching and learning strategies, including ICT, that engage students in their learning.
Communicate to a professional audience a synthesis of a current Australian teacher's professional practice.
Analyse professional teaching principles and practices, including effective teaching and learning strategies.
Incorporate in planning for learning activities a range of appropriate verbal and non-verbal communication strategies to support student engagement.
Explain the foundations of literacy and numeracy teaching and learning, and design effective strategies for their application and differentiation in teaching areas.
Apply knowledge and skills related to research, and examine professional practices for teaching core literacy and numeracy skills.

title: Suicide Prevention
school: School of Nursing, Paramedicine and Healthcare Sciences
syllabus_overview: This subject investigates the underlying factors associated with suicide, suicide attempts and the skills required to effectively respond. It also focuses on community responses through suicide prevention. Of particular focus will be the issue of suicide prevention as it relates to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities and to ensure that suicide prevention is integral to community business. Important policies and legal and ethical responsibilities will be examined to ensure students can play an active role in their own communities to assist with the prevention of suicide.
learning_outcomes: Explore and critique through social media and lived experiences, the myths and misconceptions around attempted suicide and suicide.
Examine and discuss the definitions, theories and misconceptions of suicide and self-harm.
Critically discuss models of suicide prevention and risk management including the role of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander community and support services.
Critically describe the significance of cultural issues as they relate to suicide and self-harm.
Analyse and demonstrate promotion, prevention and early intervention strategies as they relate to suicide prevention.
Examine the indicators and risk factors leading to suicide.
Critically discuss legal and ethical issues as they relate to suicide prevention and intervention.

title: Succession Law
faculty: Faculty of Business, Justice and Behavioural Sciences
school: Australian Graduate School of Policing Security
